items.title: FG gives Benin-Asaba concessionaire conditions to continue work
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — The Federal Government has given the Benin-Asaba Expressway Concession Company (BAECC) three options on the way forward with the construction of the Benin-Asaba Highway, following widespread concerns over the deteriorating condition of the road. The development came 24 hours after the Federal Government apologised to Nigerians over the hardship being experienced by motorists using the highway. The 125-kilometre highway was concessioned to BAECC in 2025 and is expected to be completed in September 2027. Speaking at a stakeholders’ meeting convened by the Minister of Works, David Umahi, at the Government House, Benin City, the Minister said three reputable contractors had been assembled to take over the construction if BAECC agreed to the proposed terms. Umahi said the first option was for the concessionaire to be given the right of first refusal to operate and toll the road after the Federal Government completes the construction, allowing it to recover its investment. The second option, he said, was termination of the concession agreement due to existing disputes, with all relevant stakeholders duly informed. The third option was for BAECC to engage a competent contractor already operating in Nigeria, while the Federal Government would take responsibility for the design and supervision of the project. Under the third option, Umahi said BAECC would retain the right to toll the highway and receive 70 per cent of the revenue, while the Federal Government would receive 30 per cent. The Minister described the options as a generous offer, stressing that the government was prepared to take necessary steps to address the situation. “We are available for trouble,” he said. Umahi said the concession agreement had placed the government in a difficult position and warned that there would be consequences for whichever decision was eventually taken. “By the concession agreement, we played into the hands of the concessionaire. There are implications of any decision we take. It is up to the concessionaire to lower his pride,” he said. He directed the BAECC chief executive officer to withdraw from the project site, while the Independent Engineers would assess all work executed, excluding what he described as “negative work.” “We want to plead, we do not see you having the capacity to fix the road. Allow the Ministry of Works to bring in competent contractors. You have no technical capacity. It is a highly technical job. It will require committed personnel,” Umahi said. He urged BAECC to provide written approval for the ministry to bring in competent contractors, warning that the government could not allow the deteriorating condition of the road to lead to public disorder. The Minister said the concessionaire was not being asked to abandon the project but directed it to remove unprofessional personnel from the site. He also listed a number of corrective measures, including reinstating all removed asphalt at the concessionaire’s cost, removing water flowing onto the carriageway, restoring free flow of traffic and removing the project director whose qualifications, he said, were in doubt. Other directives included providing evidence of previous road construction experience, removing unsuitable materials used as stone base and submitting a technical design for storm-water channelisation. Umahi also accused BAECC of several defaults, including failure to comply with instructions from the Independent Engineers, refusal to remove allegedly unqualified personnel, destruction of national assets, inadequate equipment, engaging allegedly incompetent engineers and demonstrating inadequate knowledge of road construction. He further accused the concessionaire of creating public disorder and abandoning the project site without notifying the relevant authorities. Governor Monday Okpebholo expressed concern over the condition of the highway, saying the state of the road was unacceptable after 16 months of work. “What we are seeing now is not what we are supposed to be seeing after 16 months. You cannot give what you do not have,” the governor said. He urged the concessionaire to demonstrate its capacity to execute the project, adding that Edo residents were watching developments closely. “Do the needful. Edo people are watching. Something has to be done between now and Christmas. I believe in what people will see. You cannot make profit where you are not working. There has to be a laid-down principle,” Okpebholo said. Responding, the Head of Legal, BAECC, Peterson Fabian, described the Federal Government’s proposals as friendly and collaborative. He appealed for more time to enable the company consult with its partners and hold further discussions before deciding on the way forward. Chairman of the Senate Committee on Works, Senator Allwell Onyesoh, described the condition of the Benin-Asaba Highway as terrible and said the situation had exposed the need for greater scrutiny of concession agreements in Nigeria. “The concessionaires and whoever pushed for this concessionaire did not mean well for Nigeria, and this is a big lesson about concessionaires in Nigeria. We can see that it is not everybody that has the capacity to handle such a big project,” he said. The post FG gives Benin-Asaba concessionaire conditions to continue work appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: APL demands forensic probe into GoldBod following $1.7billion gold-trading losses
items.description: The Africa Policy Lens (APL) is calling for an immediate forensic investigation into the Ghana Gold Board (GOLDBOD), following disclosures in the IMF’s August 2026 report that Ghana lost more than US$1.7 billion in gold trading under the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP). According to the IMF report, almost all of the losses were linked to purchases of gold doré. While the losses are recorded on the Bank of Ghana’s books, APL says GOLDBOD’s central role in sourcing and off-take makes it impossible to ignore the Board in any probe. “GOLDBOD was responsible for sourcing operations in 2025. The draft further relies on sections 2 and 3(2) of the Ghana Gold Board Act in describing the Board as Ghana’s sole gold trader,” APL stated in a release on Wednesday August 26, 2026. The IMF identified three main factors leading to the loss: Service and assay fees paid to GOLDBOD, discounts granted to off-takers/exporters and forex spreads – the gap between the forex bureau rate used to buy gold and the cedi reference rate used by BoG for accounting The IMF puts total DGPP costs losses for 2025 at approximately 17% of the value of gold traded APL’s review, the statement noted, found that GOLDBOD fees and off-taker discounts accounted for about 1.758 percentage points, with the bulk coming from foreign exchange spreads. “Where significant quantities of artisanal and small-scale mining gold are purchased through a state-backed system with substantial purchasing powers and public financing, any reported losses amounting to approximately 17% of the value of the gold concerned demand an urgent review,” APL said. 8 key concerns raised by APL APL argues the issue goes beyond which institution recorded the loss and made a nunber r of observations captured in theor report as follows: Concentrated powers: In 2025 GOLDBOD had purchasing authority, tax privileges, state-backed financing, and regulatory powers all in one. FX exposure: With GOLDBOD positioning itself as a major source of foreign exchange, the costs of generating that FX must be scrutinized. Cost gap: The IMF projects DGPP costs will fall to 5% in 2026, from 14.5% historically and 11.4% in Q1 2026. APL is asking: what exactly changed to drive that drop? International benchmark: The World Gold Council cites an illustrative cost of 1.87% based on Ecuador’s model, far below Ghana’s 14.5% in 2025. “APL’s assessment therefore identifies GOLDBOD’s purchasing and pricing model as an area of significant potential risk within Ghana’s gold-trading architecture,” the think-tank said. 6-Point Demands With GOLDBOD set to assume full , with costs borne by Government, APL is pushing for urgent reforms and has made 4 demands as follows: Comprehensive review of GOLDBOD’s purchasing and pricing model audit aggregator operations, commissions, premiums, and verify value for money. Independent oversight mechanism to monitor pricing, volumes, and provide regular reconciliation to prevent conflicts of interest. Publication of off-taker agreements including discount rates and commercial justification. Review of GOLDBOD’s dual role — consider making it primarily a regulator while licensed private firms handle commercial trading to reduce state financial exposure. Separation of mandate clearly distinguish gold bought for strategic reserves from gold bought for FX trading, with separate funding and accounting. Forensic examination now – failure to act, APL warns, “could expose Ghana to further financial risks in 2026 and beyond.” The APL adsed that failure to examine the purchasing and pricing model and, in particular, the factors that contributed to the reported 2025 losses could expose Ghana to further financial risks.

items.title: Nicolas Jackson à Aston Villa : le cadre idéal pour se relancer ?
items.description: Après des débuts remarqués à Chelsea puis une période plus compliquée, marquée par un prêt à Bayern Munich et une place de plus en plus marginale dans le projet de Xabi Alonso, Nicolas Jackson s'apprête à tourner une nouvelle page de sa carrière. Selon Fabrizio Romano, il devrait prendre la direction Aston Villa, où plusieurs éléments laissent penser que l'attaquant sénégalais a toutes les cartes en main pour retrouver son meilleur niveau. Aston Villa n'est plus le club en reconstruction d'il y a quelques années. Sous l'impulsion d'Unai Emery, les Villans se sont installés parmi les cadors de la Premier League, avec une qualification en Ligue des Champions et un titre en Ligue Europa qui témoignent de la trajectoire ascendante du club. Ce projet ambitieux s'accompagne d'une politique de recrutement intelligente, capable d'attirer des joueurs à fort potentiel et de les faire progresser dans un système de jeu exigeant et bien huilé. Un vivier qui fait exploser les talents Le club du Midlands a une réputation solide en matière de développement de joueurs. Plusieurs attaquants et milieux offensifs (Watkins, Rogers, Tielemans, Onana…) ont vu leur cote grimper spectaculairement une fois passés entre les mains du staff villan, portés par une méthode de travail rigoureuse et un contexte compétitif stimulant. Pour un joueur comme Nicolas Jackson, en quête de continuité et de confiance, intégrer un effectif où l'exigence rime avec progression individuelle pourrait être exactement ce dont il a besoin. Emery, un allié de poids Au-delà du projet collectif, c'est la relation entre Nicolas Jackson et Unai Emery qui pourrait faire toute la différence. Les deux hommes se connaissent bien depuis leur passage commun à Villarreal, où l'entraîneur espagnol avait suivi de près l'éclosion du jeune Sénégalais. Cette confiance mutuelle est un atout rare dans le football moderne : Emery sait exactement comment exploiter les qualités de vitesse, de percussion et de mouvement de Jackson, et l'attaquant, de son côté, retrouve un technicien en qui il a une confiance totale. Un timing qui tombe bien Avec le départ annoncé d'Ollie Watkins vers l'Arabie Saoudite, Aston Villa a besoin d'un renfort offensif immédiat et fiable. Jackson arrive donc dans un contexte où il sera attendu, mais aussi où il aura toute la place pour s'exprimer et redevenir un titulaire indiscutable. Entre un club ambitieux, un système qui a fait ses preuves pour révéler des talents, et un coach qui connaît déjà ses forces sur le bout des doigts, Nicolas Jackson a clairement toutes les conditions réunies pour rebondir à Aston Villa. Oumar Boubacar NDONGO

items.title: Atiku’s fuel subsidy position shows policy flip-flops — Presidency
items.description: — Accuses ex-VP of lacking understanding of his proposed policy By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The Presidency has criticised former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, over his position on petrol subsidy, accusing him of political posturing and policy inconsistency. The Presidency said Atiku was “suffering from a lack of basic understanding of his newfound policy prescription.” In a statement issued by the Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Mr Bayo Onanuga, the Presidency said the former vice-president’s argument appeared to misunderstand the dynamics of the petroleum market. It argued that petrol does not become cheaper simply because the government introduces a subsidy or because competition is expected to emerge. The statement said Atiku’s recent comments had raised questions about the consistency of his proposed policy on petrol subsidy. According to the Presidency, Nigerians had heard three different explanations within a week about what an Atiku administration would do regarding the subsidy. It said Atiku’s spokesperson, Paul Ibe, initially stated that Atiku would restore petrol subsidy if elected president and later phase it out, describing the measure as a temporary intervention to allow Nigerians and businesses to recover. The Presidency said another senior aide, Phrank Shaibu, subsequently described Ibe’s statement as an “unauthorised and misleading characterisation” of Atiku’s position. It added that Atiku later intervened, insisting that his position “has not changed” and that he would restore what he described as a “targeted subsidy” if elected president. Atiku was quoted as saying, “I will restore a targeted subsidy and put purchasing power back in the hands of Nigerians.” The Presidency said the development went beyond semantics, describing it as a policy contradiction that required clarification. It questioned why one of Atiku’s aides described the proposed subsidy as temporary and subject to a phase-out, while another publicly rejected the explanation before Atiku himself reaffirmed the original position. The statement said Nigerians deserved clarity rather than what it described as “policy by trial and error.” On the economics of fuel pricing, the Presidency argued that petrol prices were influenced by several factors, including international crude oil prices, exchange rates, refining costs, transportation, distribution and other market costs. It said competition could improve efficiency and margins but could not shield Nigeria completely from global crude oil prices and other input costs. The Presidency also challenged what it described as an oversimplification of the relationship between petrol prices, transportation and food inflation. It acknowledged that energy and transportation costs affect food prices but said petrol prices alone did not account for food inflation. According to the statement, agricultural productivity, insecurity, exchange rates, logistics, storage, flooding, input costs, money supply and supply constraints also influence food prices. It said a comprehensive economic programme should address these factors rather than attribute the entire cost-of-living crisis to petrol prices. The Presidency challenged Atiku to explain what he meant by “targeted subsidy”, including its projected cost, beneficiaries, funding mechanism and the conditions that would determine its eventual termination. It said Nigerians could not afford another costly subsidy regime without clear details on how it would operate. The Presidency also urged Atiku to present what it described as a coherent, costed and workable petroleum policy, rather than “playing politics” with a policy it said had improved the fiscal position of the three tiers of government and helped stabilise the macroeconomic environment. It further criticised what it described as policy inconsistency and election-driven populism, saying the economy was too important to be subjected to “policy somersaults, incoherence, destructive populism and election gimmicks.” On Atiku’s proposal to link subsidy to the crude oil barrel, the Presidency questioned whether the former vice-president had considered the other products obtained from crude oil refining. It said petrol accounts for about 45 per cent of the products from a refined barrel, while other products include aviation fuel, kerosene, diesel, petrochemical feedstocks, asphalt, hydrocarbon gas liquids, lubricants and waxes, petroleum coke and sulphur. The statement noted that diesel was deregulated in 2004 under the Obasanjo-Atiku administration, while kerosene and jet fuel were deregulated at different times. It questioned whether Atiku would also subsidise other petroleum products if his argument was based on subsidising products derived from crude oil. The Presidency also asked whether refineries receiving discounted crude would be allowed to profit from the remaining products while subsidy support was concentrated on petrol. It concluded by accusing the former vice-president of lacking sufficient understanding of the policy he was proposing. “The former vice-president is definitely suffering from a lack of basic understanding of his newfound policy prescription,” the statement said. items.title: Benin-Asaba Road: Umahi orders arrest of contractors removing asphalt
items.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Minister of Works, Engr. David Umahi, has criticised the concessionaire handling the Benin-Asaba Highway over the slow pace of work and ordered the arrest of any contractor found removing asphalt from existing carriageways. Umahi gave the directive on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, during an on-the-spot assessment of the 125-kilometre road following complaints from road users and host communities about the hardship caused by the ongoing construction. The development was contained in a statement signed by the Ministry’s Director of Information and Public Relations, Mohammed Ahmed, in Abuja on Wednesday. The Minister faulted the Benin-Asaba Expressway Concession Company Limited (BAECC) for the slow pace of work and alleged disregard for engineering standards despite repeated warnings from the Independent Engineer, Yolas Consultants, and the Ministry. Umahi said the concessionaire’s construction methodology was adversely affecting road users, host communities and the pace of work. “You are not adhering to engineering best practices in road construction and your methodology is adversely impacting road users, host neighbourhoods and the pace of work,” he said. The Minister rejected explanations by BAECC Managing Director, Mr Samuel Daramola, who attributed the difficulties to heavy traffic and double rainfall maxima along the corridor. Umahi described the explanations as “unprofessional and untenable excuses” and apologised to Nigerians for the hardship caused by the condition of the road. He directed Federal Controllers of Works and Engineering Representatives to arrest any contractor found completely removing asphalt from an existing road. “I, therefore, direct all Federal Controllers of Works and Engineering Representatives to, henceforth, arrest any contractor who completely removes the asphalt from an existing road,” he said. To ease the traffic situation, Umahi said a competent contractor would be engaged immediately to rehabilitate the critically bad portions of the highway. He also assured road users that President Bola Tinubu “feels their pains.” Chairmen of the Senate and House Committees on Works, Senator Allwell Onyesoh and Hon. Akin Alabi, respectively, described the situation as “an unacceptable disaster” and promised a nationwide review of concession agreements to ensure compliance. The Presidential Senior Special Assistant on Community Engagement, South-South, Mrs Gift Johnbull, said the President was aware of the plight of road users and had directed that solutions be found. Governor Monday Okpebholo also appealed for patience, saying a solution had been found by the Minister to address the problem. The Benin-Asaba Highway runs from AIF Roundabout in Benin City to Summit Junction in Asaba, linking the South-East, South-South and parts of the South-West. It is one of the pilot projects under the Highway Development and Management Initiative (HDMI). The Federal Executive Council (FEC) approved the concession of the highway to BAECC on a 25-year Design, Finance, Build, Operate and Transfer (DFBOT) basis in January 2023. The agreement was signed in May 2023, while the project was handed over in March 2025, with a 36-month construction period scheduled from April 2025 to April 2028. The inspection team also assessed two sections of the Benin-Sapele-Warri Road being handled by the Edo State Government on behalf of the Federal Government. The 23-kilometre section being handled by CBC Global is 75 per cent complete, while the 10-kilometre Section I, Phase 2, being handled by CCECC, is 25 per cent complete. Both sections are being constructed with Continuous Reinforced Concrete Pavement. The Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), Dr Samuel Ogbuku, pledged to reconstruct a failed 15.4-kilometre stretch between the Edo-Delta border. Umahi subsequently directed the NDDC and Federal Government project teams to harmonise their efforts on the affected sections. items.title: 14 infants killed in fire at Pims' gynae ward in Islamabad
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Fourteen infants were killed in a fire that broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) early on Wednesday. What has happened so far: 14 babies die after fire erupts in ward; initial reports say spark erupted from AC, blaze spread due to oxygen points Bereaved families decry rescue teams arrived “too late”; witnesses report locked doors Health secretary removed ; inquiry panel formed on PM’s orders; separate fact-finding committee constituted Health Minister Mustafa Kamal vows accountability ; Tallal Chaudhry defends district administration Condolences from across the nation, other countries pour in Footage showed rescue workers using ladders to reach broken windows to access the affected area and grief-stricken women sitting on the ground outside the hospital. An AFP reporter saw a woman in tears and a man clear glass from two broken windows, as security guards stood at the entrance to the medical facility. Several witnesses, their hands and faces blackened from the smoke, told AFP they waited hours for help from the emergency services. They were forced to smash through windows to try and get to the neonatal intensive care unit. Others said they came across locked doors and alleged guards prevented those inside the building from leaving as the fire raged. However, the hospital disputed this in a statement issued later in the evening. “All emergency exits were fully open and operational,” it asserted. In a statement, the Islamabad administration said that the fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital’s ward. It said that rescue teams rushed to the scene, with six fire brigade vehicles and four ambulances taking part in the rescue operation. “The fire was immediately brought under control and the children were immediately shifted to the intensive care unit,” it said, adding that 14 children “were completely burnt”. Pims Spokesperson Dr Aneeza Jalil told Dawn that 15 babies were in the ward. “At least one baby was saved by a doctor,” she said. Health Minister Mustafa Kamal, who reached Islamabad from Karachi in the afternoon, vowed that “no one responsible for negligence, including me, will be spared”. “The tragic fire incident at Pims MCH Centre, resulting in the loss of precious neonatal lives, is deeply heartbreaking,” the public hospital said. Citing a preliminary report, the Pims statement said the incident was “initially caused by a spark inside nursery at 06:38am and within seconds a massive fire erupted due to oxygen points at each incubator”. It said two doctors and two nurses on duty inside the nursery responded “immediately and called security staff, who joined in and tried to get in twice [to bring] babies out until 06:39am, when a huge blast occurred and ceilings fell down”. The statement said the duty staff managed to rescue a baby in the nursery and four in an adjacent room, along with three mothers. “Besides immediate response, staff managed rescue of 73 other admitted patients in the adjacent Gynae ward on the same floor within minutes,” it added. The hospital asserted that “available fire safety equipment installed, including 35 fire extinguishers, were all utilised by the staff to contain the situation”. Health minister vows accountability Speaking to reporters in Islamabad, the health minister said he will present himself to his superiors for accountability. Providing details of the incident, Kamal said: “At 6:38am, it can be seen in the CCTV footage that there was a spark in the AC, then a fireball could be seen erupting out of it and landing on the floor of the ward. In one minute, at 6:39am, four people, including two nurses and two doctors, could be seen rushing for help and around the same time, the whole room was engulfed in flames”. The health minister said the incident was being investigated by “experts, different institutions including us”, adding that “nothing will remain hidden and all facts will be unearthed”. He continued: “Apparently, it seems that 14 out of the 15 infants were connected to oxygen tubes and it was that oxygen which caught flame.” Kamal reiterated that the “heart-wrenching” incident will be investigated and warned that “if there was any negligence, then as I said, we will not spare them, including myself”. The minister further said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had instructed him “not to speak about certain issues”. He said he would be meeting the premier and that the two had been in touch. “Everyone is on board, and the findings will be presented,” he said. On being asked if he was going to tender his resignation, the health minister said, “As I have said before, whoever is responsible [..] they will not be spared. I have said what I can, and I wish I could say more, but the prime minister is my boss, and whatever his orders will be, I can only say that.” The federal minister was also questioned about fire safety standards at Pims, with a reporter pointing out that the hospital had been issued notices for the past eight years. Kamal claimed that the hospital had ensured compliance each time a notice had been issued in the past, pointing out that the blaze was contained with “26 fire extinguishers available in the building”. When a reporter asked about his early morning statement over the lack of adequate facilities at Pims and “why in his 2-2.5 years as a health minister, no improvement had been made”, the minister, getting visibly frustrated, said, “If it has been 2-2.5 years, then feel free to shoot me” and clarified that he had only been at his position for one year and two months. “What I said in the morning has to be seen within a certain parameter. I was saying that even if this did not happen, there are still challenges at the hospital. It has a capacity of 200-300 OPDs, and today, it has a footfall of over 9,000 people”. He maintained that he was merely presenting facts. “I am not saying that everything is ideal.” When pointed out that it was his responsibility to upgrade the facility, Kamal acknowledged his role and said, “We have to do it, but things cannot be ideal given the current scenario, but if we go into that, the conversation will take a different turn”. The minister reiterated that every responsible person will be held accountable. “If I am willing to present myself for accountability, then no one else is left. “Wherever there has been negligence, we will fix it,” he said. Noting that such an incident should not have happened, he said: “Will get to its root cause and ensure prevention in the future.” The minister was also asked about reports that the door of the ward was locked, to which he said that access to the ward was limited and guarded due to “instances of people stealing newborn babies a couple of years back”. “You would not see that anywhere else in the world, but we have the issue, so the door had to be manned with a guard,” Kamal explained. During his media talk, the minister got into a verbal altercation with an individual who asked when action would be taken against those responsible. As the individual got louder, the minister repeatedly gestured to him to come forward and said, “Sir, come here and talk to me.” ‘Give me my child back’ Malik Israr, whose niece was admitted to the gynae ward, told Dawn that it was unfortunate the nursery was housed in a building in which repair and renovation work was ongoing. “After the fire erupted, they told patients to vacate the building. Women who had just given birth had to rush down the stairs from the second floor,” he said. A worker removes broken pieces of a glass window after a fire broke out at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — Reuters Khurram Mehmood, 40, told AFP he lost his three-day-old daughter in the blaze and that rescuers took hours to arrive. “I lost my daughter. She was only three days old,” he said. “My wife was in the ward. They took everyone out. We were sitting on the road waiting for help.” He added, “The fire erupted at 6am, rescue and authorities reached at 9am; people were helping themselves.” “Give me my child back,” Jaweria, who lost her newborn, said outside the hospital. “I want justice.” She told AFP : “Rescue teams arrived too late. Police arrived after four hours and said they are here to investigate. To hell with you, rescue team and police. Babies burnt to death there, but nobody could save them.” A grieving father reacts as his child’s coffin is transported in an ambulance following a fire outside the Mother and Child Health (MCH) ward at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) Hospital in Islamabad on August 26, 2026. — AFP “For two hours I kept crying and wailing,” the mother said, questioning the action taken by hospital staff and emergency responders. “Why did the doctors leave the children there? One nurse, one doctor, one gynaecologist, one paediatrician — there was nobody in the entire ward. Why were they not there?” Mudasir, another parent who also lost his child, said all doors of the ward, except one, were shut and that there was “no fire security” in the ward. A mother with black residue from the smoke on her hands stood crying outside the hospital as she held her 10-day-old baby in her arms. “People were screaming. There was black smoke. We ran for our lives. Thank god my baby is safe,” Shagufta Parveen told AFP . A man consoles a grieving father (C) as his child’s coffin is carried after a fire outside the Mother and Child Health (MCH) ward at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) hospital in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — AFP Ali Abbas, 20, was with his sister who was a patient in the ward. “There was a short circuit in the nursery, in the children’s ward,” he said. “It was full of smoke.” Eyewitness Abdul Ghafoor told AFP that there was “thick black smoke inside and patients were trapped”. “I barged in to try to save as many people as I could, but we could not reach the ward where the patients were. “The fire was in the nursing room, and we could not see anything. Some of us broke the windows to help people get out.” Among the victims were the twin daughters of Bahadur Khan, a vegetable seller, The New York Times reported . He had left them with their mother to get some rest at home. Bahadur said his wife was recovering in Pims’ intensive care unit and was not aware of the deaths of their three-day-old daughters. Alam Zaib, the father of a newborn child who was in another ward and remained safe, was quoted as saying that he tried to enter the ward where the fire broke out, but the door was locked. Pims, established in 1985, is Islamabad’s biggest public sector hospital. It is one of the oldest health facilities in the federal capital and comprises several hospitals and teaching institutes. Fires in large buildings are frequent in Pakistan, often due to poor safety laws and building codes as well as lax enforcement. Health secretary removed; inquiry, fact-finding panels formed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice of the incident and directed the relevant authorities to investigate it. According to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), he expressed deep sorrow and grief at the incident and offered his condolences to the bereaved families. “Such a situation involving children is unbearable,” the statement quoted him as saying. “The circumstances that led to the incident should be thoroughly reviewed, those responsible should be identified, and the strictest possible action should be taken,” he said. In a second statement, the PMO said the prime minister had suspended and removed federal Health Secretary Muhammad Aslam Ghauri. The premier chaired a high-level meeting on the incident, where he expressed his anger and issued directives for “strict action”, the PMO said in another statement. It also stated that the prime minister suspended the federal health secretary and asked him to leave the meeting. The statement quoted the prime minister as saying: “I am heartbroken at this tragic incident and share the parents’ grief.” Subsequently, Captain (retired) Muhammad Mahmood, a BS-21 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), was appointed to the post of health secretary for three months “or till the posting of a regular incumbent,” a notification issued by the Cabinet Secretariat said. According to the PMO, a high-level inquiry committee, headed by former interior secretary Shahid Khan, has launched an investigation. According to state-run Radio Pakistan , Major General (retired) Dr Khursheed Uttra, Establishment Division Secretary Dr Barrister Nabeel Awan and Islamabad Deputy Commissioner Irfan Nawaz Memon will serve as its members. The inquiry committee will submit an interim report to the prime minister within 48 hours, containing recommendations for immediate action. It will submit a comprehensive report within five days, containing the findings of the complete investigation and actionable recommendations. The health ministry has been directed to immediately notify the inquiry committee and provide it with the necessary assistance. According to the terms of reference (ToRs), the panel will ascertain the cause of the fire and review the rescue operations carried out by the hospital staff and relevant agencies such as Rescue 1122. Besides conducting a detailed review of the fire safety infrastructure at Pims, the committee will also determine the responsibility and negligence, if any, of individuals involved in the incident. It will recommend necessary reforms for Pims’s administrative system to help prevent such kind of incidents in the future. Separately, a notification issued by the Islamabad district magistrate said that a seven-member fact-finding committee, headed by the additional deputy commissioner general (ADCG), had been formed to determine the facts behind the fire. The members of the committee included the CES director general, the City police station superintendent, the assistant commissioner (Industrial Area), the director general of Capital Development Authority’s (CDA) Electrical and Mechanical wing, along with representatives from Pims and Islamabad Electric Supply Company. The committee was tasked with determining the exact cause of the fire, assessing whether adequate and functional fire-safety measures were in place, and evaluating the response time and effectiveness of the rescue and fire-fighting operations. The notification said that a report would be furnished within 24 hours. Ambulances are parked outside a mortuary following a deadly fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on August 26, 2026. — AFP Minister of State for Law Barrister Aqeel Malik assured in a post on X that a “complete, transparent, and impartial investigation of the incident will be conducted to determine the true causes of this catastrophe and any possible negligence”. “In the event that negligence or failure is proven at any level, strict action will be taken against the responsible individuals in accordance with the law,” he added, extending his condolences to the bereaved families and expressing grief over the incident. Meanwhile, PPP leader Nayyar Hussain Bokhari, who reached Pims along with Senator Sherry Rehman and others, demanded that the head of the MCH be removed. Bokhari said it was not just negligence but rather criminal negligence and should not be ignored. Rehman said the Pims’ executive director must “answer why the system here keeps being akin to gross negligence”. “The health ministry now has no justification for taking public funds. It should be dissolved or devolved to the provinces,” she was quoted as saying by her party. She insisted they were not visiting “to play politics” but were sent by the party leadership to raise questions on behalf of the public. In a post on her X account, Rehman also shared a video of her visiting the ward. “Totally gutted. People had to break windows and jump out. Emergency gate was closed, fire equipment not working, medical staff not present,” she wrote. “Honestly, I would have resigned on the spot,” Rehman added later. Tallal Chaudhry defends district administration Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry insisted that there had not been any delay in the arrival of rescue teams and defended the district administration. “After receiving information in the control room, they reached the hospital within six minutes,” the state minister said while speaking to the media in Islamabad. He added that once the rescue teams assessed the situation, 19 people were rescued, including seven children, 1o mothers and two men. He also said that administration officials “from the assistant commissioner to commissioner to the Islamabad IG” reached the hospital to monitor the situation. “Not only did they monitor but also assisted in the rescue operation,” he said. Reiterating that rescue teams reached the site within six minutes, the state minister said, “There appears to be no negligence on the part of rescue services.” However, he added, only the hospital administration could answer for the arrangements present within the hospital. Chaudhry said that the bodies of all 14 infants had been handed over to their families. He added that a report of the incident had been sent to the prime minister and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who he said had been monitoring the situation. On being asked if Pims met the CDA’s fire safety protocols, with a journalist also pointing out that his ministry had been issuing notices to the hospital for the past seven years, he acknowledged that notices had been issued. “It is a huge institution, and notices were issued […] but what was complied with and what was not — as there are multiple buildings; we cannot conclude anything today, and an inquiry committee has been formed”. Asked why the administration had not been active on the fire safety issue before, he said, “If there has been any negligence, the inquiry committee will find out.” An inquiry committee has been formed for a “high-powered” investigation into the incident, Chaudhry noted. He said the committee will collect evidence — CCTV footage, presence of flammable equipment, why the door was locked, the number of doctors and nurses present — and present its findings. In its update on the incident, CDA said fire and rescue teams reached the site within seven minutes after a call was received at 6:54am. Fire tenders, rescue teams, ambulances of the Capital Emergency Services (CES) and the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) administration were part of the deployed resources. Nation expresses grief President Asif Ali Zardari expressed heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the bereaved families. In a statement, the president said that the loss of lives was “heartbreaking and an irreparable loss”. “Responsibility for the incident should be determined and action should be taken in accordance with the law,” he said. Effective fire safety and emergency arrangements must be ensured in hospitals for the protection of patients, especially newborn babies, the president urged. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said he was deeply saddened by the incident. “My deepest condolences to the bereaved parents and families. No words can ease the pain of losing an innocent child. May Allah Almighty grant the families strength and sabr in this unimaginably difficult hour,” he said. As per the prime minister’s orders an immediate and thorough investigation will establish the causes of this tragic incident to ensure that those found responsible face the strictest action. The safety of our children must remain paramount,” he said. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari wrote on X: “Mothers do not keep their children in the womb for nine months just so that, due to someone’s negligence, they burn alive as soon as they are born. “The deaths of 14 newborns in the federal capital are one of the most horrific tragedies in human history. The helpless fathers, whose lamps of hope were extinguished the very instant they were lit, are seeking justice.” In a statement earlier in the day, he described the incident as an “unbearable tragedy for the entire nation”. He called for an impartial investigation into the incident and said the nation be informed how such a tragedy occurred at a major hospital. “Those responsible for negligence or failing to ensure the safety of patients must be held accountable,” he added, stressing that the federal government must ensure the safety of patients and medical staff at all hospitals under its administration. First Lady and MNA Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari also expressed “profound grief and sorrow over the tragic loss of newborn babies” and conveyed her “deepest sympathies to the bereaved families”. “The loss of innocent newborn lives is heartbreaking and deeply distressing,” a statement by the Presidency quoted her as saying. She called for a “thorough, swift and transparent investigation” into the incident. PML-N President Nawaz Sharif said he was “deeply grieved” to hear about the deaths. He urged the government to take strict action against those responsible and ensure measures were put in place to prevent such incidents in the future. Senate Chairman Syed Yousuf Raza Gilani expressed deep grief and sorrow over the tragic incident. In a statement, he offered his condolences to the families affected. He said effective safety measures, fire safety systems and all necessary arrangements to deal with emergencies must be ensured in hospitals to prevent such incidents. “Any negligence in safety measures is unacceptable,” he said. Gilani urged the relevant authorities to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the incident and take effective and practical steps to prevent such tragedies in the future. National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq also expressed profound grief and sorrow over the deaths of the infants. In a statement, he said he was “heartbroken” over the incident and shared equally in the pain and grief of the bereaved parents. United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund (Unicef) called for an urgent review as it expressed grief over the incident. “Unicef is deeply saddened by the tragic loss of at least 14 newborn lives following a fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad today. “We extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved families and all those affected by this devastating incident,” it said in a statement. The UN agency added, “ Every newborn deserves a safe start to life, and every mother and child should be able to receive care in a safe, secure health facility. It called for the urgent review and strengthening of fire prevention and safety standards across health facilities. The British High Commission in Pakistan termed the incident “heartbreaking news”. “Our deepest condolences and thoughts are with the parents and families at this unimaginably difficult time,” it said. Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Ministry also expressed “deepest condolences and sincere sympathy” to the families of the infants and to the people and the government of Pakistan. “The kingdom expresses its solidarity with the families of the victims and stands with the government and people of Pakistan in the face of this great tragedy, wishing the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and its brotherly people security and peace,” the statement read. The Turkish embassy said it was “deeply saddened by the tragic loss of newborn lives”, “We extend our heartfelt condolences and deepest sympathies to the bereaved families. Our thoughts and prayers are with them at this profoundly painful time. May Allah grant them strength, patience and solace,” it said on X. Spain’s embassy also extended heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. “Our thoughts are with all those affected by this heartbreaking tragedy.” The French embassy shared the sentiment, describing the incident as “deeply distressing”. “Our hearts go out to the families who lost their newborn children in the tragic fire at Pims in Islamabad. Loss of innocent lives is heartbreaking and deeply distressing. Embassy of France extends its deepest sympathies to bereaved families and everyone affected by this tragedy,” it said in its message on X. The Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) said in a statement that it was in “deep mourning” over the incident. “The association reiterates that healthcare facilities are designed to protect and restore human lives, yet administrative failure and regulatory oversight lapses have turned these institutions into danger zones,” it said. It demanded action against officials “whose failure to uphold safety codes resulted in this catastrophe”. It also demanded enforcing strict consequences so that “systemic failure serves as a decisive warning, preventing future lapses across both public and private medical facilities”. It further said that there should be immediate restructuring and public accountability of health regulatory authorities responsible for enforcing safety protocols, building codes and emergency infrastructure in hospitals. The PMA also called for “full institutional backing for the grieving parents, ensuring they receive complete legal, financial, and emotional justice”. Search for Justice (SFJ) and Children Advocacy Network (CAN) Pakistan, a collective platform of local civil society organisations working for the protection and rights of children, also expressed their deep sorrow. “The death of newborn children in a place entrusted with their treatment and care is deeply distressing and raises serious questions about safety and emergency preparedness,” said Rashida Qureshi, programme manager at SFJ and spokesperson for CAN Pakistan. In its statement, the Islamabad Citizens Network (ICN) said, “This is not merely an unfortunate accident; it is a national tragedy in which innocent newborns, entirely dependent on the hospital system, its staff and state-provided arrangements for their safety and survival, lost their lives.” It contended that an inquiry committee headed by an ADC was “neither adequate nor appropriate given the gravity of the tragedy and the need to determine possible administrative, criminal and institutional responsibility”. ICN demanded an immediate judicial inquiry and an independent investigation into allegations by parents regarding the absence of staff, emergency exits and other administrative lapses. It recalled that similar tragic incidents had occurred in Lahore’s Services Hospital in June 2012, the National Institute of Child Health (NICH) in Karachi in January 2020, and the nursery of Sahiwal Teaching Hospital in June 2024. Civil Society Network Pakistan (CSNP) called upon Federal Constitution Court’s (FCC) Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan to take immediate notice on a suo motu basis or initiate appropriate constitutional proceedings on serious human rights violations arising out of the babies’ deaths. CSNP President Advocate Abdullah Malik told Dawn that he has also requested the FCC chief justice to consider constituting a high-level, independent and transparent inquiry to determine the exact cause and circumstances of the fire at Pims. Additional input from AFP, Reuters and Nasir Iqbal

items.title: Government workers without valid NIA details risk salary suspension from September 15
items.description: Government employees whose valid National Identification Authority (NIA) details are not captured on the government payroll system risk having their salaries suspended from September 15, 2026. The directive has been issued by the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department (CAGD) ahead of a planned nationwide employee re-verification exercise. In a statement dated August 24, 2026, the CAGD directed Human Resource departments of Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to ensure that all employees have accurate NIA numbers captured in the government payroll system. The directive follows discrepancies identified after the rollout of the upgraded Employee Payslip (E-Payslip) system, which have prevented some employees from accessing their payslips. According to the CAGD, some NIA numbers currently captured on the payroll do not correspond with employees’ records at the NIA, while others have no NIA details captured on the system. “Employees who do not have valid NIA details on the payroll system will have their salaries suspended with effect from 15th September, 2026,” Controller and Accountant-General Kwasi Agyei said in a separate notice. The CAGD said the measure is intended to ensure that employee records are properly validated ahead of the nationwide re-verification exercise. Human Resource departments have consequently been directed to identify affected employees and correct their NIA numbers on the payroll. For corrections or insertion of NIA details, the affected employee’s application must be submitted together with a cover letter from the head of the institution authorising the correction or insertion. The documents are to be forwarded to the CAGD for validation. The Department has also directed Human Resource officers to check their institutions’ corporate email accounts for lists of employees flagged as having “No NIA” details and take the necessary corrective action. The CAGD further reminded employees that physical copies of NIA cards are no longer required for submission and inspection. It said this is in accordance with Regulation 9 of the National Identity Register (Amended) Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2523). Employees are instead required to ensure that their NIA numbers and other identity details are accurately captured in the government payroll system through their respective Heads of Human Resources. The CAGD has urged employees and institutions to comply with the directive before the September 15 deadline to avoid disruptions to salary payments.

items.title: 20-year-old arrested for allegedly killing father in Anambra
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu A 20-year-old man, identified as Pascal Ogbogu, has been arrested by the Anambra State Police Command for allegedly killing his 56-year-old father with a machete in Abatete, Idemili North Local Government Area of the state. Preliminary information from the Police indicated that the suspect allegedly attacked his father on Tuesday evening before fleeing the scene. Following a distress report, Police operatives from the Eziowelle Police Division, assisted by family members and members of the Abatete Vigilante, mobilised to the scene and found the deceased lying in a pool of blood with a deep machete wound on his throat. The Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), Tochukwu Ikenga, said the deceased’s body was evacuated to a mortuary for preservation and autopsy. According to him, the suspect, who fled after the incident, was arrested in the early hours of August 26, 2026, through the coordinated efforts of the Police and members of the Abatete Vigilante. Ikenga said timely information and cooperation from community members also contributed to the suspect’s arrest, as residents assisted security operatives in tracking and locating him. The Commissioner of Police, CP Nnanna Oji Ama, commended the prompt response of the security operatives and the support provided by members of the community. He particularly praised the family members, community members, Police operatives and vigilante personnel for their cooperation, stressing that community participation, timely information sharing and effective collaboration between the Police and local communities remained essential to protecting lives and property. While commiserating with the deceased’s family, the CP directed that the case be transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for further investigation and comprehensive review. He said the investigation would establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that all relevant facts were properly determined. Ama assured the family and members of the public that the investigation would be conducted professionally, thoroughly and diligently in accordance with the law, adding that the suspect would face due process upon conclusion of the investigation. The post 20-year-old arrested for allegedly killing father in Anambra appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 244 projets retenus, 570 millions FCFA mobilisés : le FDCUIC dévoile les résultats de son Appel à projets 2026
items.description: Le Conseil d'administration du Fonds de Développement des Cultures urbaines et des Industries créatives (FDCUIC) a validé, le jeudi 20 août 2026, les résultats de l'Appel à projets 2026, une échéance très attendue par les acteurs culturels du pays. Dans un communiqué parvenu à notre rédaction ce 26 aout 2026, l’organisation dévoile les résultats. L'édition 2026 aura suscité une mobilisation massive : 855 dossiers ont été déposés sur la plateforme dédiée. Après l'étape de vérification, l'établissement public précise que « 754 projets ont été déclarés éligibles et soumis à évaluation », soit un taux de recevabilité de près de 88 %. Les dossiers retenus pour l'évaluation ont ensuite été passés au crible de plusieurs critères. Selon le communiqué, l'examen a porté notamment sur « la pertinence, la qualité, la faisabilité, l'impact social et économique, le caractère innovant et la viabilité » des initiatives présentées, une grille d'analyse qui se veut exigeante et transversale. 244 lauréats pour une enveloppe de 570 millions FCFA Au terme du processus de sélection, le Conseil d'administration a arrêté sa liste : 244 projets ont finalement été retenus, pour un montant global de 555 millions FCFA. Un appui complémentaire vient s'y greffer, puisque le FDCUIC indique que 15 millions FCFA supplémentaires ont été alloués « au titre de l'appui à la mobilité artistique », un dispositif géré séparément de l'appel à projets classique. Au total, ce sont donc 570 millions FCFA qui seront injectés dans l'écosystème des cultures urbaines et des industries créatives. Une diversité de filières concernées Le Fonds souligne que les initiatives lauréates couvrent plusieurs secteurs des cultures urbaines et des industries créatives, avec l'ambition affichée de contribuer « à la création, à la professionnalisation, à la structuration et au développement » de ces filières à l'échelle nationale. Les porteurs de projets sélectionnés devront désormais patienter pour connaître les modalités pratiques de mise en œuvre. Le FDCUIC annonce que les informations relatives au conventionnement et au versement des subventions seront diffusées « prochainement » via ses canaux de communication officiels. L'établissement, placé sous la tutelle technique du ministère de la Culture, a par ailleurs adressé ses félicitations aux lauréats et remercié l'ensemble des candidats ayant pris part à cette édition 2026. O.B.N

items.title: OSP must investigate everyone in AKSA deal’s value chain – Mary Addah
items.description: Transparency International Ghana Executive Director Mary Addah has urged the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) to conduct an extensive investigation into the Ghanaian dimension of the Asante Kweku Berko bribery case, insisting that all institutions and individuals involved in the deal’s value chain should be examined. According to her, the investigation should not be limited to the five persons already identified by the OSP as persons of interest, but should extend to every individual and institution that may have handled or interacted with the project. Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Wednesday, August 26 , Ms Addah said institutions including GRIDCo and others connected to the transaction should be called upon to assist the investigation. “I think it should be very extensive. Mention institutions, including GRIDCo and others. So everybody in the value chain who may have at one point dealt with this issue has been investigated, or has been called upon to support the process,” she said. She explained that a comprehensive investigation would help establish whether individuals who were involved in the process played any meaningful role in the alleged scheme. According to her, expanding the scope of the probe does not mean everyone examined will eventually be implicated. She stressed that investigations are intended to establish the facts and either confirm, validate or disprove allegations. “Remember, investigations are either to confirm, validate, or otherwise,” Ms Addah said. She therefore believes the OSP should initially cast its net wide and subsequently exclude individuals who are found not to have played a critical role. “It doesn’t take away from the process if we expand it, and then at a second point decide to be linked and remove those who may not have played a critical role,” she explained. Ms Addah said a broad investigation would also benefit individuals and institutions that have no involvement in wrongdoing, as it would allow them to be cleared based on evidence rather than assumptions. “It’s for their own benefit as well that everybody is looked into,” she added. Her comments follow the OSP’s identification of former Power Minister Kwabena Donkor and four others as its main persons of interest in the Ghanaian aspect of the bribery case involving Asante Kweku Berko. The other persons named are Francis Walkson Kwesi Gyata, a former technical adviser to the Minister of Power; Solomon Adjetey Sowah, a former deputy director at the Ministry of Power; Lindin George Nii Mettle, a former director at Tricop Group Limited; and Baffour Ankomah Brobbey, an employee of Tricop Group Limited. The OSP’s investigation follows Berko’s conviction by a federal jury in Brooklyn, New York, on August 3, 2026, over a bribery scheme involving more than US$1 million. Berko, a former Managing Director of the Tema Oil Refinery, was convicted over allegations that he conspired to pay bribes to multiple Ghanaian officials between 2014 and 2015 in connection with the development and financing of a 370-megawatt fuel oil plant in Tema. The project involved the Government of Ghana, Turkish energy company AXA Energy Eratim and Goldman Sachs. The OSP has said it provided investigative and evidentiary assistance to the US Federal Bureau of Investigation through Ghana’s mutual legal assistance framework, with the US Department of Justice acknowledging the assistance.

items.title: Incidences de la création de nouvelles circonscriptions territoriales sur les conseils communaux, les conseils régionaux et le Parlement (Par Mamadi 3 Kaba)
items.description: Après avoir salué la création de onze préfectures et de deux régions administratives, il convient à présent d’examiner les incidences de cette réforme sur les Conseils communaux concernés , les d e ux futurs Conseils régionaux et le Parlement . I- SUR LE S CONSEILS COMMUNAUX Au préalable, il est utile de préciser que l’organisation territoriale de la République repose sur la déconcentration et la décentralisation ( article 181 de la Constitution ) . Les circonscriptions territoriales ( déconcentration ) sont : les Régions , les Préfectures et les Sous-préfectures. Les collectivités décentralisées ( décentralisation ) sont : les Régions et les Communes. De ce fait et pour une compréhension facile , un parallèle peut être établi entre les deux processus de déconcentration et de décentralisation . Ainsi, aux Sous-préfectures correspondent les Communes ( rurales ) , aux Préfectures correspondent les Communes ( urbaines ) , tandis que les Régions présentent une double dimension, à la fois déconcentrée et décentralisée. Conformément aux dispositions de l’article 231 du Code électoral , chaque Conseil communal est composé d’un nombre de membres proportionnel au nombre d’habitant de la Commune. En effet, le double scrutin (législatif et communal) du dimanche 31 mai 2026 a permis le renouvellement des Conseils des 375 Co mmunes de la République. Parmi ces Collectivités, les onze (11) Communes , correspondant aux onze (11) Sous-préfectures érigées en Préfectures, dispos ent déjà d’un Conseil régulièrement élu pour un mandat de cinq (5) ans , conformément aux dispositions de l’ article 221 du Code électoral . En conséquence, la réforme susvisée engendre l es incidences entre autres : 1. Le remplacement des Sous-préfets en fonction par des Préfets ; 2. Le nombre de Préfecture pass ant de trente-trois (33) à quarante-quatre (44) ; 3. La continuité d es mandat s en cours des Conseils et Exécutifs communaux ; 4. Pour la prochaine élection communale, l ’adaptation du nombre de membres d es C onseil s communa ux en fonction du nombre d’habitant de s Commune s . II- SUR LE S DEUX F UTURS CONSEILS REGIONAUX Suivant le processus de décentralisation, chaque r égion administrative est administrée par un Conseil régional élu . Les Conseillers régionaux sont élus au suffrage indirect, au scrutin majoritaire à un tour, pour un mandat de cinq (5) ans, renouvelable. Ainsi, chaque C onseil communal élit en son sein, un ou deux représentants devant siéger au Conseil régional. Ces élections ont lieu, au plus tard, soixante (60) jours après le renouvellement des Conseils communaux ( article 212 du Code électoral ). Certes , les Conseils régionaux ne sont pas encore élus . Il n’en demeure pas moins que la question se pose de savoir si les deux nouvelles Régions administratives seront dotées de Conseils régionaux . En effet , une lecture combinée d es dispositions du Règlement Intérieur du Sénat et celles du Code électoral permet d’établir l’existence d’une corrélation institutionnelle entre les Conseil s communaux, l es Conseils régionaux et l e Sénat. Dès lors, toute modification de l’organisation territoriale ayant une incidence s ur les Communes ou les Région s peut produire des effets sur la composition du Sénat. Ainsi , conformément à l’article 8 de la Loi organique portant Règlement Intérieur du Sénat , le nombre de Sénateur est fixé à quatre – vingt-un (81) . Subséquemment , suivant les dispositions de l’article 187 du Code électoral , les deux tiers des Sénateurs sont élus , au suffrage indirect par un collège électoral composé de conseillers communaux et de conseillers régionaux , à raison de : a. 1 Sénateur par préfecture, les 33 anciennes préfectures donnant les 33 Sénateurs ; b. 1 Sénateur par chef-lieu de région, les 7 anciennes régions administratives donnant les 7 Sénateurs ; c. 1 Sénateur pour la zone spéciale de Conakry ; d. 13 Sénateurs, dont 1 issu de chaque commune de Conakry. Les Sénateurs élus sont au nombre de cinquante-quatre (54), correspondant au x deux tiers de 81. Les Sénateurs choisis par le Président de la République sont au nombre de vingt-sept (27), correspondant au tiers de 81. Vu ce qui précède, pour que les deux nouvelles R égions administratives soient dotées des Conseils régionaux et participent à l’élection des Sénateurs, il faut des mesures entre autres : 1- Le vote d’une loi portant création de deux nouvelles Collectivités décentralisées . En effet, si la création des circonscriptions territoriales, leurs attributions, leur organisation et leur fonctionnement relèvent du domaine réglementaire ( article 182 de la Constitution ), la création des collectivités décentralisées ainsi que leur organisation relèvent du domaine de la loi ( article 183, alinéa 1 de la Constitution ). La loi ainsi adoptée érigera les deux régions administratives (Siguiri et Beyla) au rang des C ollectivités décentralisées. 2- La révision de l’article 8 de la l oi organique portant Règlement intérieur du Sénat et de l’article 187 d u Code électoral . La révision des articles des deux lois organiques permettra d’une part , de réajuster le nombre de Sénateurs et d’autre part, d’ inclure les deux nouvelles régions administratives et les onze nouvelles préfectures dans l ’élection des deux tiers des membres du Sénat. En procédant ainsi , le nombre de Sénateur s à élire se présentera comme suit : A. 1 Sénateur par préfecture, les 44 préfectures don nant les 44 Sénateurs ; B. 1 Sénateur par chef-lieu de région, les 9 régions administratives donn ant les 9 Sénateurs ; C. 1 Sénateur pour la zone spéciale de Conakry ; D. 13 Sénateurs, dont 1 issu de chaque commune de Conakry. Donc, le nombre de Sénateur à élire sera Soixante-sept (67). Au titre de s recommandation s , il serait judicieux que la zone spéciale de Conakry ait deux (2) Sénateurs à élire . En tenant compte de cette recommandation, le nombre de Sénateur à élire est porté à s oixante-huit (68) qui constitueront les deux tiers (2/3) et le tiers (1/3) sera composé de t rente-quatre (34) Sénateurs . En conséquence : – L e S énat sera composé de c ent deux (102) membres ; – Le tiers des Sénateurs est choisi par le Président de la République ; – Les deux tiers des Sénateurs sont élus par le corps électoral constitué des conseillers régionaux et communaux de chaque région du pays. III- SUR LE PARLEMENT Le Parlement est composé de deux Chambres : l’Assemblée nationale et le Sénat. Si la première représente le Peuple, la seconde représente les Collectivités décentralisées et les composantes socioprofessionnelle de la Nation. Le nombre de D éputé s à l’Assemblée nationale est fixé à 147 . L es deux ( 2/3 ) sont élus dans le cadre des circonscriptions électorales et le tiers ( 1/3 ) sur la liste nationale pour un mandat de cinq (5) ans (article 151, 153 du Code électoral ) . Nonobstant la différence entre les modes d ’ élections, chaque Député représente la Nation entière ( article 154, alinéa 5 du Code électoral ). Ainsi, le Député élu au scrutin de liste nationale à la représentation proportionnelle exerce les mêmes fonctions qu e le Député élu au scrutin majoritaire uninominal ou plurinomina l à un tour . L es fonctions de représentation de la Nation , de vote des lois, de l’évaluation des politiques publiques et de contrôle de l’action gouvernement ale sont exercées au nom et pour le compte d e la Nation tout entière . C’est pourquoi, l a création de nouvelles Préfectures et de nouvelles R égions administratives n’aura pas d’ incidence s sur la dixième (10 ème ) législature déjà en cours , aussi bien dans la composition de l’Assemblée nationale que dans la représentati vité . En outre, l ’érection de s onze (11) nouvelles P réfectures en circonscriptions électorales est un autre préalable à remplir . Si la circonscription territoriale renvoie à la notion d’organisation du territoire, la circonscription électorale quant à elle, renvoie à la représentation politique à travers l ’organisation d es élections. ​​ Mercredi 26 août 2026 MAMADI 3 KABA ​​​​​​​ Juriste – Facilitateur BRIDGE L’article Incidences de la création de nouvelles circonscriptions territoriales sur les conseils communaux, les conseils régionaux et le Parlement (Par Mamadi 3 Kaba) est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Tribute to the late Kwabena Kesse (Stephen Boateng) from the May 9 Foundation and its president, Mr. Herbert Mensah
items.description: It is with a profound sense of shock and sorrow that the May 9 Foundation and I, Herbert Mensah, learn of the sudden passing of our dear friend and steadfast pillar of support, Lawyer Stephen Boateng, known to the world as Kwabena Kesse or Kessben. Our hearts are heavy with grief, and we extend our deepest condolences to his family, the wider Kessben Group family, the legal fraternity, and all who were touched by his remarkable life. The news of his death on Wednesday, August 19, 2026, in Kumasi, marks the end of an era for Ghanaian business and philanthropy. For the May 9 Foundation, Mr. Kesse’s loss is particularly personal and immense. He was not just a donor; he was one of the foundation’s original and most consistent champions. From the very inception of our mission in 2001, following the horrific Accra Sports Stadium disaster, Mr. Kesse stood with us. He was a source of strength, providing unwavering support that has been a cornerstone of our work for a quarter of a century. His belief in our cause, which began as a mission to honor the 126 souls lost and support their families, helped us grow into a movement that now touches countless lives across Ghana. Whether it was through direct financial contributions, providing resources for our annual remembrance walks, or ensuring our charity events were a success, Mr. Kesse’s commitment was absolute. His name appears among the earliest and most consistent supporters in our history, a testament to his character and his belief in our shared humanity. For 25 years, he was a quiet but powerful force, helping us provide mobility aids, essential supplies, medical assistance, and life-changing heart surgeries to hundreds of Ghanaian children who had nowhere else to turn. Our work would not have been possible without his loyalty and generosity. Beyond his philanthropy, Mr. Kesse’s journey from a schoolteacher to the founder of a vast business empire—spanning media, hospitality, education, and finance—was an inspiration. He represented the very best of the Ghanaian spirit: resilience, intellect, and a profound sense of duty. His legacy, however, will be the lives he touched, not just through his businesses but through his kindness and unwavering support for the most vulnerable among us. Kwabena Kesse was a true friend, a pillar of the community, and a man who lived by the belief that we must always remember and we must always help. His absence leaves a void that will be deeply felt. We have lost a brother, and our foundation has lost a founding father. The May 9 Foundation and I pledge to honour his memory by continuing the work he so passionately believed in. May his soul rest in perfect peace. Herbert Mensah President, May 9 Foundation

items.title: Ouagadougou : L’Association Jeunes Faiseurs de Paix mobilise les quartiers pour prêcher la paix
items.description: Face aux défis qui ébranlent le Burkina Faso, l’Association Jeunes Faiseurs de Paix (AJFP) mise sur la jeunesse pour recoudre le lien social. Après l'arrondissement 11, la preuve par l’exemple a été donnée dans le 12e arrondissement de la capitale, où une caravane citoyenne a semé les graines d’un avenir apaisé. Le 25 août 2026 restera une date symbolique pour les habitants du 12e arrondissement de Ouagadougou. Ce jour-là, en effet, l’Association Jeunes Faiseurs de Paix (AJFP) y a fait escale dans le cadre de son initiative itinérante dédiée au vivre-ensemble. Une neuvième halte qui, loin d’être anodine, visait à transformer ce quartier en un laboratoire de coexistence pacifique. Plusieurs notabilités coutumières et religieuses ont pris part à la caravane Devant une assistante composée de représentants de l’administration, de sages coutumiers, de guides religieux et d’une jeunesse nombreuse, les échanges ont tourné autour de la paix. L'objectif de l'AJFP est d'endiguer la défiance qui mine les relations communautaires. Selon les premiers responsables de l’AJFP, il ne s’agit pas de faire de la figuration. L’ambition est clairement est d'inciter les autorités traditionnelles et spirituelles à passer de la parole aux actes, en multipliant sur le terrain des gestes concrets de rapprochement. Hermann Guingané, qui préside aux destinées de l’association a insisté sur la confiance comme ciment de toute nation. « Chaque fois qu’on ose se parler, un mur d’incompréhension s’effondre. Et quand la méfiance cède la place à l’estime mutuelle, la paix cesse d’être un vœu pieux pour devenir une réalité palpable », a-t-il lancé, avant d’enjoindre ses compatriotes à faire preuve de vigilance face aux sirènes de la division. « Le Burkina a soif d’unité. Il attend de chacun de ses enfants qu’ils tournent le dos aux rancœurs, aux stéréotypes et à toutes ces petites habitudes qui érodent notre capacité à faire bloc », a précisé Hermann Guingané. Le point d’orgue de cette journée a été la mise en place d’un comité local de paix, entièrement composé de jeunes volontaires issus des différents secteurs de l’arrondissement. Une photode famille Leur mission est d'incarner la continuité du projet en devenant des ambassadeurs du dialogue au quotidien, bien après le départ de la caravane. « Une caravane, par sa nature, est éphémère. Elle peut sillonner un quartier en quelques heures, mais elle ne saurait se substituer aux habitants pour construire leur propre destin. C’est à eux de s’emparer de cet élan », a souligné M. Guingané. Cette philosophie trouve un écho favorable chez Zalissa Paré, la présidente de la délégation spéciale locale. Félicitant l’initiative, elle a rappelé que la quiétude publique n’est pas l’affaire des seules forces de l’ordre ou des politiques. « La sérénité s’obtient par un effort collectif et quotidien. Elle exige l’implication de toutes les strates de la société, sans exception », a souligné la PDS Paré. items.title: Bouaddi becomes most expensive EPL teenager after Man City move — see top 10
items.description: Manchester City’s signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille has rewritten the record books for teenage transfers in the Premier League. The 18-year-old Morocco international has joined City in a deal worth up to £86 million, comprising a reported £81.3m initial fee and £4.3m in add-ons. The move makes Bouaddi the most expensive teenager ever signed by a Premier League club, overtaking Manchester United’s Leny Yoro. Here is the list of the most expensive teenagers signed by Premier League clubs: 1. Ayyoub Bouaddi — Lille to Manchester City — £86m Bouaddi has taken the top spot after City agreed a deal worth up to £86m for the 18-year-old midfielder. The Morocco international emerged as one of the brightest young midfielders in Europe after breaking into Lille’s first team at just 16. He made 30 Ligue 1 appearances last season and also featured prominently for Morocco at the 2026 World Cup. 2. Rasmus Højlund — Atalanta to Manchester United — £72m Manchester United signed Danish striker Rasmus Højlund from Atalanta in 2023 for a reported £64m initial fee, with the deal potentially rising to around £72m. Højlund was 20 when he moved to Old Trafford and arrived after a breakthrough season in Italy. 3. Romeo Lavia — Southampton to Chelsea — £53m Chelsea beat Liverpool to the signing of Romeo Lavia in 2023, paying Southampton around £53m for the Belgian midfielder. Lavia had impressed during Southampton’s relegation season and was regarded as one of the Premier League’s most promising young midfielders. 4. Leny Yoro — Lille to Manchester United — £52.2m Before Bouaddi’s arrival, Yoro held the record for the most expensive teenage signing by a Premier League club. Manchester United paid Lille £52.2m for the French centre-back in 2024, with the fee potentially rising further through add-ons. 5. Raheem Sterling — Liverpool to Manchester City — £49m Sterling was 20 when Manchester City signed him from Liverpool in 2015 for an initial £44m, with the deal potentially reaching £49m. The England international went on to become one of City’s most successful attackers, winning four Premier League titles, five League Cups and an FA Cup. 6. Anthony Martial — Monaco to Manchester United — £36m Manchester United signed Martial from Monaco in 2015 when he was 19. The initial fee was around £36m, with performance-related clauses capable of taking the overall package significantly higher. Martial scored on his debut against Liverpool and enjoyed several productive spells at Old Trafford. 7. Luke Shaw — Southampton to Manchester United — £31.5m Shaw was only 18 when United signed him from Southampton in 2014 for around £27m, with the deal potentially rising to £31.5m. He had already established himself as one of the Premier League’s leading young full-backs before making the move. 8. Gabriel Jesus — Palmeiras to Manchester City — £27m Manchester City agreed a deal worth around £27m for Gabriel Jesus in 2016, when the Brazilian forward was 19. He arrived in England after establishing himself as one of Brazil’s brightest young attacking talents. 9. Fabio Silva — Porto to Wolverhampton Wanderers — £35m Wolves paid Porto around £35m for Silva in 2020, making the 18-year-old one of the most expensive teenagers in Premier League history. The Portuguese forward was viewed as a major prospect when Wolves made the investment. 10. Joe Cole — West Ham to Chelsea — £6.6m Chelsea signed Cole from West Ham in 2003 when he was 21, meaning he does not technically qualify as a teenager. For an accurate teenage-only list, he should therefore be excluded.
