items.title: Tarkwa residents petition government to renew Gold Fields mining leases
items.description: Residents and representatives of communities hosting Gold Fields Ghana Limited’s Tarkwa Mine have petitioned the government to renew the company’s five mining leases before they expire in April 2027. The petition, addressed to the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources through the Minerals Commission, calls for an early decision on the renewal application to provide certainty for the mine, its employees, contractors and businesses that depend on its operations. The residents said their appeal was informed by their experiences as assembly members, teachers, youth leaders, contractors, traders, farmers and other community members who have witnessed both the benefits and challenges associated with mining in the Tarkwa area. According to the petition, Gold Fields submitted its application for the renewal of the leases in November 2025 and is seeking an extension beyond the current lease period. The residents are urging the government to complete the statutory, technical, environmental and commercial assessments of the application and, if the company satisfies all applicable requirements, approve the renewal ahead of the April 2027 expiry. They said an early resolution would help safeguard jobs, sustain local businesses and enable communities and other stakeholders to plan with greater certainty. The petitioners also stressed the importance of continuity in the operations of the Tarkwa Mine, given its significance to the local economy and the livelihoods of residents and businesses within its host communities. They are therefore appealing to the government to expedite the necessary processes and take a decision on the renewal application within the remaining period before the leases expire. They argue that uncertainty over the future of the mine could affect investment decisions, employment and economic activity in Tarkwa. The petition cites Gold Fields’ published 2024 operational figures, which it says recorded 568 employees and 5,092 contractors at the Tarkwa operation, with 71 per cent of its workforce drawn from host communities. The residents further point to the Gold Fields Ghana Foundation’s social investments, saying the Foundation had invested more than US$110 million in projects and programmes serving communities around the Tarkwa and Damang mines as of 2025. They mention investments in education, health, water and sanitation, agriculture and infrastructure, including roads, the redevelopment of the Tarkwa and Aboso Stadium and a girls’ dormitory at HUNIVAS. The petition also makes a case for the mine’s environmental performance. While acknowledging that community investment should not excuse environmental non-compliance, the residents say they have witnessed rehabilitation of mined-out areas and restoration of wildlife habitats during visits to the concession. They are therefore asking government to consider the company’s employment, social investment and environmental management record as part of the lease-renewal process. Renewal debate The petition comes against the backdrop of growing public debate over the future of the Tarkwa mine. On July 24, 2026, a section of the Apinto Divisional Council called on government not to renew Gold Fields’ leases and instead proposed that the operation be handed over to a Ghanaian-owned mining company. The petitioners acknowledge that position but argue that it should not be treated as a unanimous view of communities in the Tarkwa mining area. They cite a May 30, 2026 appeal by chiefs and residents of Huniso for the President to renew the Gold Fields lease. The petition says Huniso hosts more than 70 per cent of the Tarkwa Mine. The residents supporting the renewal also reject what they describe as a false choice between Gold Fields’ continued operation and increased Ghanaian ownership of the mining sector. They argue that a renewed lease could instead be used by government to secure stronger commitments on Ghanaian participation, including local procurement, employment, skills transfer, enterprise development and community benefits. What the petitioners want The residents are asking government to expedite the assessment and negotiations over the five leases and, subject to the company meeting the relevant legal and regulatory requirements, approve the renewal well before April 2027. They are also calling for stronger commitments from the company on host-community employment, local procurement, skills development, environmental rehabilitation and local enterprise development. The petition invokes the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), particularly provisions governing the extension of mining leases. It ultimately asks government to base its decision on the law, regulatory compliance, economic considerations, environmental performance and the interests of host communities. The petition was signed on behalf of the residents and host communities by the Assembly Member for New Atuabo, Hon. Nsor, and community representative Nana Kwasi Ansah of Huniso. The renewed debate now leaves government with the task of weighing competing positions from stakeholders in Tarkwa as it considers the future of one of Ghana’s major mining operations. The current leases are due to expire in April 2027. Petition to the Minister of LNR Download

items.title: NRSA to deploy Traffictech to apprehend traffic offenders, introduce mandatory towing to curb crashes
items.description: The National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) is to deploy Traffictech, a technology-based system to monitor motorists and apprehend those who violate traffic regulations. Mr Abraham Amaliba, Director-General of the NRSA, said the system would use cameras and other monitoring devices installed at strategic locations to identify traffic offenders. He said unlike the traditional approach where police officers stood at vantage points to identify and arrest offenders manually, Traffictech would use technology to improve enforcement. Mr Amaliba was speaking on behalf of Mr Joseph Bukari Nikpe, Minister of Transport, at the Ghana Logistics and Transport of the Chartered Institute of Logistics and Transport (CILT) Conference and Annual General Meeting in Fiapre, near Sunyani in the Bono Region. He said cameras would be mounted on poles, while others would be placed on tripods and vehicles. “Traffictech is about using technology to apprehend persons who don’t obey traffic rules,” he said. He said about 16 traffic offences would be captured under the system. Mandatory towing system Mr Amaliba also announced plans to introduce a mandatory towing system to reduce crashes caused by broken-down vehicles. He said the Ministry had identified broken-down vehicles as a leading cause of road crashes, particularly when they remained stationary on the road. Under the new law, expected to be rolled out next year (2027), every vehicle owner would be required to register or subscribe to a towing company or an insurance company. “When your car breaks down, all you need to do is call your subscriber, and they will come and remove it,” he said. Mr Amaliba said a dedicated towing platform, similar to a ride-hailing platform, would connect motorists to the nearest registered towing company. He said all towing companies would be required to register with the NRSA before they could operate under the new system. He said the Authority would undertake a nationwide public education campaign to create awareness about the new law. Call for inclusive transport Alhaji Saaka Dumba, President of CILT Ghana, called for a transport system that took into account the needs of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups. He said although Ghana had signed international treaties and enacted laws on the rights of persons with disabilities, implementation remained a challenge. “Look at our vehicles, the trotros, and even supposed government vehicles. They are high-entrance buses. They don’t have low-floor buses where somebody can put a wheelchair and just go inside,” he said. Alhaji Dumba said public transport operators should provide vehicles with ramps, low floors and other features that would allow persons with disabilities to board and travel with ease. He called for deliberate planning to ensure that persons with disabilities were considered when vehicles were purchased, and transport infrastructure was developed. “We think that transport should be integrated,” he said. According to the 2024 Ghana Statistical Service report cited at the conference, public transport options such as shared minibuses lacked wheelchair ramps, designated seating and other facilities for persons with disabilities. It also identified high-floor vehicles, poorly maintained sidewalks and the absence of traffic signals with audio prompts as challenges affecting the movement of persons with disabilities. Gender inclusion Mrs Doreen Owusu-Fianko, Global Chairperson of Women in Logistics and Transport (WiLAT), commended institutions working to promote gender inclusion in the logistics and transport sector. She urged other institutions to adopt measures that would give women greater opportunities to participate and advance in the industry. The three-day CILT Ghana Logistics and Transport Conference and Annual General Meeting was held from August 25 to 27, 2026, under the theme: “Transforming Ghana’s Transport Infrastructure for Inclusive and Sustainable Growth.” The conference is discussing urban transportation and traffic congestion management, public-private partnerships in road transport development, and inclusive transport systems for persons with disabilities and vulnerable groups. CILT Ghana was established and registered in 1965 as a professional body with branches in Accra, Tema, Kumasi, Takoradi and Sunyani.

items.title: « En choisissant de ne pas adhérer à l’Éco, la Guinée a réaffirmé sa volonté de protéger son indépendance économique » (Fondation Ahmed Sékou Touré)
items.description: À l’occasion de la commémoration du 25 août 1958, date historique associée au discours d’Ahmed Sékou Touré face au général Charles de Gaulle, la Fondation internationale Ahmed Sékou Touré pour la paix (FIAST) a célébré ses 12 années d’existence à travers une conférence de presse organisée mardi à la Maison de la presse, à Conakry. La rencontre a réuni des camarades de lutte, des représentants de la nouvelle génération révolutionnaire ainsi que des invités venus d’ailleurs. Au-delà de la portée historique de cette commémoration, les échanges ont particulièrement mis en lumière une question au cœur des débats sur la souveraineté africaine : l’avenir monétaire de la Guinée et son rapport au projet de monnaie Éco. Dans son intervention, l’administrateur général de la FIAST, Ibrahima Sory Camara, a salué la position des autorités guinéennes, qu’il présente comme une affirmation de l’indépendance économique du pays. « Nous saluons avec enthousiasme et satisfaction les efforts accomplis par Monsieur le Président de la République et son gouvernement pour leur engagement en faveur de la préservation de la souveraineté monétaire de notre pays. » Pour la Fondation, le débat sur l’Éco ne saurait être réduit à une simple question technique ou financière. Il s’inscrit dans une réflexion plus large sur la capacité des États africains à maîtriser leurs instruments économiques et à décider librement de leur trajectoire de développement. « En choisissant de ne pas adhérer au projet d’adoption de l’Éco, la Guinée a réaffirmé sa volonté de protéger son indépendance économique, en rappelant qu’une monnaie nationale constitue l’un des piliers fondamentaux de la souveraineté d’un État et un symbole fort de son autonomie politique et économique. » Cette prise de position intervient dans un contexte où la question de la souveraineté monétaire occupe une place croissante dans le débat panafricain. La monnaie est notamment perçue par certains acteurs comme un instrument déterminant de la politique économique, de la capacité d’investissement et de la définition des priorités nationales. Pour la FIAST, la défense de la souveraineté monétaire s’inscrit ainsi dans la continuité de la réflexion engagée autour du « Non » guinéen de 1958 : celle d’un État qui entend disposer de la liberté de déterminer ses choix politiques, économiques et stratégiques. Dans cette même logique, la Fondation a également salué les efforts du ministère de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat en faveur de la préservation du patrimoine national, notamment à travers le lancement des travaux de construction des musées régionaux. « Bien plus encore, nous félicitons le ministère de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat, en particulier Monsieur le Ministre, M. Moussa Moïse Sylla, pour les efforts remarquables déployés dans le cadre du lancement des travaux de construction des musées régionaux. Cette initiative historique témoigne d’une volonté affirmée de préserver, de valoriser et de transmettre notre patrimoine aux générations présentes et futures. Car le musée constitue la mémoire vivante d’une nation et symbolise l’éternité de son histoire, de sa culture et de son identité. » En célébrant ses douze années d’existence, la FIAST a également appelé les Guinéens à faire de la culture, de l’unité et de la paix des leviers du développement national. « La FIAST, gardons à l’esprit que notre culture est notre identité, notre unité est notre force, et la paix demeure la condition indispensable de notre progrès collectif. Cette commémoration doit être comme un appel à la conscience collective de tous les Guinéens pour préserver la paix, renforcer l’unité nationale, valoriser nos cultures et bâtir ensemble une société fondée sur la dignité et la solidarité. » Ainsi, 68 ans après le discours historique du 25 août 1958, la question de la souveraineté demeure au centre du récit porté par la Fondation. De la liberté politique à l’indépendance économique, le débat autour de la monnaie Éco apparaît, pour ses responsables, comme l’une des expressions contemporaines de cette quête de maîtrise du destin national et africain. Mayi Cissé L’article « En choisissant de ne pas adhérer à l’Éco, la Guinée a réaffirmé sa volonté de protéger son indépendance économique » (Fondation Ahmed Sékou Touré) est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Veteran actress Grace Nortey dies at 89
items.description: Veteran Ghanaian actress Grace Nortey, one of the pioneers of the country’s theatre, television and film industry, has reportedly died at the age of 89. Nortey reportedly passed away in the early hours of Wednesday, August 26, 2026, at the University of Ghana Medical Centre (UGMC). Born on February 1, 1937, the celebrated actress had a career spanning more than five decades, becoming one of the most recognisable faces of Ghanaian entertainment. She was particularly known for portraying strong-willed, outspoken and commanding female characters, earning her the popular nickname “Maame Gyata,” meaning Lion Woman or Lion Lady. Nortey was active in some of Ghana’s most popular television and theatre productions, including Obra, Osofo Dadzie, Key Soap Concert Party, Cantata, Taxi Driver and Thursday Theatre. Her major screen debut came in the 1986 comic film Juju, produced by King Ampaw and Peter Wohlgemuth-Reinery, where she played the wife of veteran actor Joe Eyison. She went on to feature in several Ghanaian productions, including Nana Akoto, The Other Side of the Rich, Escape to Love, Matters of the Heart, Expectations, Jewels, The Ties That Bind and Sinking Sands. Her career also extended to international productions. She appeared in the 2015 Netflix film Beasts of No Nation, directed by Cary Joji Fukunaga and starring Idris Elba and Abraham Attah. She played the role of the Old Witch Woman in the film, which was shot in Ghana. Beyond acting, Nortey worked as a Senior Administrative Assistant with the Ghana Education Service and was an advocate for the welfare of veteran actors. Her contribution to Ghana’s creative industry earned her several honours. She won Best Cameo Actress at the Ghana Movie Awards in 2011 for Adams Apple and received the Excellence in Arts award at the Glitz Women of the Year Honours in 2016. In 2018, she received a Lifetime Achievement Award at the Black Star International Film Festival. She was also honoured with a Legendary Award for Outstanding Contributions at the Ghana Actors Entertainment Award in 2020. In 2021, she received an Outstanding Contribution to Women’s Excellence in the Performing Arts honour at the 3Music Awards Women’s Brunch, while she was honoured again in April 2025 during the Ashanti Festival for her contribution to Ghanaian entertainment. Nortey was married to the late Daniel Nortey, and the couple had five children, including actress Sheila Nortey. In her later years, she reduced the number of demanding acting roles she accepted due to mobility and eyesight challenges. She had previously explained that reading lengthy scripts had become difficult, although she remained open to smaller roles that allowed her to work from scenarios and improvise. Details of the cause of her death have not been publicly disclosed. Grace Nortey’s reported passing marks the loss of a veteran performer whose career connected Ghana’s early radio, theatre and television era with the modern film industry.

items.title: Anambra LG Poll: APGA set to contest unopposed in 20 LGAs
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — The All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) is set to contest Saturday’s local government election in 20 of the 21 local government areas of Anambra State, with opposition parties failing to field candidates in the affected councils. The only council where a contest is expected is Anambra East, where a candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP) is challenging the incumbent local government chairman. Speaking at a campaign rally for the election in Otuocha on Wednesday, Governor Chukwuma Soludo attributed the absence of opposition candidates to what he described as their assessment that challenging APGA would amount to a waste of resources. Soludo said the outcome of the 2025 governorship election, in which he claimed to have secured 73 per cent of the votes, contributed to the decision by other political parties not to participate in the council poll. “Anambra is a fortress of APGA. Following my 73 per cent score during the governorship election, other political parties felt there is no need for them to waste their money in Saturday’s local government election and that is why they ran away,” he said. The governor said with no opposition candidates in 20 LGAs, voters in those councils would effectively be affirming the APGA candidates. “In 20 out of the 21 LGAs, no party fielded any candidate and so in those LGAs, the people will just be doing affirmation because it is democracy. “In 20 LGAs, no party is challenging APGA and proper election will take place only in Anambra East. Anambra is APGA and APGA is Anambra and so, none of them wanted to waste their time and money,” Soludo said. The governor also highlighted some of his administration’s programmes, including free education, free antenatal and delivery services, youth empowerment and recruitment into the health and education sectors. He said more than 300,000 women had benefited from the state’s free antenatal and delivery programme, while over 16,000 youths had been trained and empowered under the “One Youth, Two Skills” initiative. Soludo added that the state had recruited 1,500 medical personnel and more than 8,000 teachers as part of efforts to strengthen primary healthcare and education. “We’re on massive acceleration in all the sectors,” he said. On the 2027 general elections, Soludo said APGA was already preparing for the contests, adding that the party would unveil its candidates at the appropriate time. “After booting, we launch and when we launch, it will be tsunami. Anambra is APGA land. “We will unveil our presidential candidate, the senatorial, House of Representatives and House of Assembly candidates at the fullness of time,” he said. Soludo said the party would commence its campaign for the general elections at the appropriate time, adding that the state would support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the presidential election as part of efforts to sustain collaboration with the Federal Government. “Our campaign for general elections will come, but you know that apart from the presidential election which will go to our president, others will go to APGA. “We will vote for the president so that we will continue with our collaboration because there are so many things in the offing, which will enable us get our share from the Federal Government,” he said. The post Anambra LG Poll: APGA set to contest unopposed in 20 LGAs appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ghana rejected MTN’s GH¢20m donation to sustain diplomatic pressure on South Africa – Int’l Relations Analyst
items.description: International Relations analyst Dr Ishmael Hlovor says Ghana’s decision to decline a GH¢20 million donation from MTN Ghana for victims of xenophobic attacks in South Africa is part of a broader diplomatic strategy to maintain pressure on the South African government. According to him, while accepting the donation could make economic sense and provide support to affected victims, rejecting it sends a stronger diplomatic message to South Africa that Ghana considers the recurring attacks on foreigners a serious issue requiring sustainable solutions. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Wednesday, August 26, Dr Hlovor said Ghana wants South Africa to openly engage with the issue and take responsibility for addressing the conditions that continue to facilitate xenophobic attacks. “I think that it’s just a continuation of what Ghana intends to do about this regular attack on foreigners in South Africa. That is ensuring that you bring much more diplomatic pressure [on] the South African government and let South Africa engage openly to provide sustainable solutions to the issue of xenophobic attacks,” he said. His comments come after Ghana declined a GH¢20 million donation offered by MTN Ghana to support Ghanaian victims of recent xenophobic attacks in South Africa. Dr Hlovor explained that accepting the donation could allow South African authorities and businesses to portray themselves as supporting victims, while avoiding a deeper conversation about their responsibility to condemn and address the attacks. Dr Hlovor described the proposed donation as potentially forming part of what he called “backdoor channels” aimed at helping South Africa manage the damage to its international image. “Ghanaians are not willing to allow South Africa to use backdoor channels to try and clean its image,” he stated. He noted that South African authorities had previously called on other African countries to bear the cost of repatriating their citizens affected by the attacks. Against that background, he said, it would be difficult to separate donations by South African-linked entities from broader diplomatic and reputational considerations. “The same South African government is calling on other African nations to pay for repatriation of their citizens, and then you have the South African entities who are now trying to donate to countries that have suffered from the xenophobic attack and who have put a lot of resources into repatriating their citizens,” he said. Dr Hlovor stressed that the issue therefore goes beyond the immediate financial benefit of the GH¢20 million. He said that from an economic perspective, accepting the money may appear sensible because it could assist victims and communities affected by the attacks. However, from an international relations perspective, declining the offer could help Ghana sustain diplomatic pressure for a more permanent solution.

items.title: Un «nouveau crime de guerre» de Kiev : trois blessés, dont un enfant, dans une attaque contre Donetsk
items.description: Le centre de Donetsk a ete la cible de frappes ukrainiennes le 26 août, a declare Denis Pouchiline, dirigeant de la Republique populaire de Donetsk (RPD). Selon lui, des impacts d'obus ont ete signales dans un quartier densement peuple de la ville. a la suite de ces bombardements, au moins trois personnes, dont un enfant, ont ete blessees a des degres divers. Denis Pouchiline a qualifie l'attaque ukrainienne de « nouveau crime de guerre » commis par le regime de Kiev, qui « ne cesse jamais de montrer sa vraie nature terroriste par ses frappes contre des zones civiles pendant les heures de pointe ». Selon l'agence TASS, au moins quatre explosions se sont produites dans le centre de Donetsk. Une fumee a ete observee pres du grand centre commercial Donetsk City, a proximite duquel se trouvent des immeubles residentiels de cinq et neuf etages. D'apres un specialiste du Comite d'enquete russe, des fragments, vraisemblablement issus de munitions de gros calibre de fabrication etrangere, ont ete decouverts lors d'une inspection des lieux. Il a ajoute que ces fragments seraient collectes et envoyes pour analyse afin de determiner leur nature et le type de projectile. Le meme jour, le regime de Kiev a frappe un autocar de ligne assurant la liaison Lissitchansk-Stakhanov, en Republique populaire de Lougansk (RPL). a la suite de cette attaque, qualifiee par le dirigeant de la RPL, Leonid Passetchnik, de nouvel acte de terrorisme « cynique, inhumain et injustifiable », au moins neuf personnes sont mortes, dont huit sur le coup, et une jeune femme de vingt ans est decedee en reanimation malgre les efforts des medecins. Au moins six personnes ont ete blessees, dont la mere de la jeune femme decedee en reanimation, ainsi qu'une jeune fille de 18 ans qui a ete hospitalisee. Le Comite d'enquete russe a ouvert une enquete penale pour attaque terroriste.

items.title: ‘My statement taken out of context’ – Kuje chairman clarifies
items.description: The Chairman of Kuje Area Council, Samuel Shekwolo, has said some of his recent remarks that sparked public backlash were “taken out of context,” insisting that they did not reflect his intentions or the official position of his administration. Shekwolo had come under criticism after he threatened to send away anyone who refuses to vote for the All Progressives Congress in the upcoming elections, prompting backlash from members of the public. The chairman made the clarification during a press conference while responding to reactions to the controversial remarks. “In public governance, clarity, truth and transparency are essential. In recent days, certain statements made were taken out of context and leading to a distorted narrative that do not reflect my true intents or core values or the official position of this administration,” he said. While acknowledging the role of the media in a democratic society, Shekwolo urged journalists to consider the context of statements before publishing them. “While I respect the press and its vital role as a pillar of our democracy, it is crucial to clarify the intent of the message,” he said. Shekwolo explained that the remarks were made in a specific context while addressing issues relating to administrative efficiency, local development and community welfare. “The remarks were made in a specific context aimed at addressing administrative efficiency, local development and community welfare. You may recall that the events that led to the unfortunate meeting was a meeting with APC party and loyalists,” he said. He also said he had no intention of violating the fundamental rights of residents in the council. “I have no right to any resident or citizens of their fundamental human rights in the council,” he said. Shekwolo added that his administration remained committed to inclusive governance, equity and the development of all communities in Kuje Area Council. “Let me state sincerely that our administration remains fully committed to inclusive government, equity and total progress of every community in Kuje Area,” he said. “At no point did I intend to cause disaffection, undermine any group or promote policies that do not serve the best interest of our citizens,” he added. The council chairman urged residents, regardless of their political, religious or ethnic affiliations, to support efforts aimed at developing the area. “I urge the people of Kuje Area Council and general public regardless of their political affiliation, religious or ethnic differences to join hands with our administration to make Kuje Area the council of our dreams,” he said. He also called on journalists to uphold professional standards by verifying the context of statements before publication. “I urge the media to maintain high standard of professional journalism by verifying contexts before publications because we are partners in partners. Our doors remain open for constructive dialogue and feedback,” Shekwolo said. The post ‘My statement taken out of context’ – Kuje chairman clarifies appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: World Bank backs Ghana’s recovery, urges sustained reforms
items.description: The World Bank says Ghana must complete structural reforms to sustain its economic recovery and translate growth into jobs. It commended Ghana’s six per cent economic growth and the reduction in inflation from 23.2 per cent in 2023 to 3.2 per cent in March 2026, but cautioned that persistent vulnerabilities could undermine long-term sustainability. The World Bank Division Director for Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone, Dr Robert Taliercio O’Brien, said this at the Ghana 10th Economic Update, launched in Accra under the theme: “ Reset for Growth: Sustaining Macroeconomic Recovery and Unlocking Transport for Transformation .” He said Ghana had entered 2026 at an inflection point, with the immediate challenge being to convert macroeconomic gains into employment and fiscal stability. He said the Government’s policy decisions had contributed to the improved economic performance but cautioned that Ghana was “not out of the woods yet”, with sustained fiscal consolidation requiring stronger revenue systems. Dr O’Brien questioned the durability of the recovery, saying policy choices made in the near term would determine whether the gains translated into lasting economic transformation or remained vulnerable to external shocks. He said recent growth had been concentrated in gold and services, sectors that had limited capacity to absorb labour relative to Ghana’s demographic growth. The World Bank official said 36.4 per cent of Ghanaians remained outside the formal tax system, constraining the Government’s capacity to finance public services and infrastructure. He called for structural transformation centred on job-rich growth, particularly in agriculture, agro-processing and manufacturing, where productivity and labour absorption could be increased. Dr O’Brien said the World Bank would continue to support Ghana’s economic transformation and job creation, but stressed that financial resources alone would not be sufficient without political commitment and institutional capacity. The Finance Minister, Dr Cassiel Ato Baah Forson, said in a speech read on his behalf that the strong headline growth had yet to benefit a significant proportion of the population. He said the Government was therefore focused on infrastructure investment and poverty reduction, with transport infrastructure expected to support broader economic activity and job creation. Dr Forson said the Government did not intend to maintain capital spending cuts indefinitely, but would restore investment as fiscal conditions improved while maintaining policy discipline. He said Ghana was seeking to consolidate its economic recovery through disciplined implementation, strategic transport infrastructure and sustained partnerships aimed at converting macroeconomic stability into jobs, food security and broader prosperity. The Minister said the Government remained committed to working with institutions such as the World Bank to strengthen economic resilience and address infrastructure gaps.

items.title: Mali : Les FAMa neutralisent des cibles terroristes à Kidal et Sévaré
items.description: L’armée malienne a mené deux frappes successives contre des groupes armés terroristes, lundi et mardi 25 août 2026, dans les régions de Kidal et de Mopti. Des véhicules armés et du matériel de guerre ont été détruits. L’État-Major Général des Armées (EMGA) a annoncé, dans un communiqué publié ce mercredi 26 août, la poursuite des opérations de sécurisation menées dans le cadre de l’opération Dougoukoloko. Les Forces armées maliennes (FAMa), appuyées par leurs partenaires, ont intensifié leurs missions de surveillance et de contrôle du territoire. Selon le communiqué, des frappes aériennes ou d’artillerie ont été réalisées sur la base de renseignements précis. Le lundi 24 août, des regroupements de terroristes ont été localisés à Abéibara, dans la région de Kidal. Ces positions, qui abritaient « d’importants matériels de guerre » et des véhicules armés, ont été « traitées avec succès ». Le lendemain, mardi 25 août, un nouveau rassemblement d’éléments armés a été repéré à 34 kilomètres au nord-est de Sévaré, dans la région de Mopti. Après analyse de la situation, la position identifiée a également été ciblée et frappée. L’EMGA précise que les opérations de surveillance et de reconnaissance se poursuivent dans les secteurs concernés. L’objectif est d’évaluer précisément les effets des frappes, d’établir un bilan consolidé et de neutraliser toute menace résiduelle. Dans son message, l’État-Major réaffirme « la détermination des FAMa à poursuivre, avec rigueur, professionnalisme et engagement, les opérations de sécurisation sur l’ensemble du territoire national ». items.title: Mercato : Crystal Palace dit non à Liverpool pour Ismaïla Sarr !
items.description: Le dossier Ismaïla Sarr continue d'agiter le mercato anglais, et Liverpool s'invite désormais dans une liste de courtisans déjà bien fournie. Après Manchester United, Galatasaray et Al-Hilal, ce sont les Reds qui ont manifesté leur intérêt pour l'attaquant sénégalais de Crystal Palace cet été. Selon les informations relayées par le journaliste Fabrizio Romano, Liverpool a formulé ce 26 aout 2026 une offre avoisinant les 58 millions d'euros (un peu plus de 38 milliards FCFA) pour s'attacher ses services, dans l'optique de renforcer son secteur offensif sur les ailes. Mais du côté des Eagles, la réponse a été sans appel. D'après The Athletic, Crystal Palace a repoussé cette première approche et ne semble pas disposé à revenir sur sa position. Le club londonien considère Sarr comme son meilleur élément de la saison écoulée et n'envisage pas de le laisser filer à ce stade du mercato, sauf offre nettement supérieure. Les Reds devront donc améliorer leur offre s'ils veulent obtenir gain de cause. La situation reste toutefois à double tranchant : si Crystal Palace veut conserver son joueur, l'intéressé, âgé de 28 ans, souhaiterait de son côté quitter Selhurst Park avant la fin du mercato. O.B.N Crystal Palace have rebuffed an initial approach from Liverpool for Ismaila Sarr. Liverpool discussed a move for Sarr as their search for a right-sided winger continues and the Palace attacker was identified as a player of interest until it became clear his current club were not… pic.twitter.com/thRgzwCsov — The Athletic | Football (@TheAthleticFC) August 26, 2026

items.title: Heritage Christian University launches LLB programme with focus on practical legal education
items.description: Heritage Christian University (HCU) has launched its Bachelor of Laws (LLB) programme through the newly established Heritage School of Law, offering prospective law students a new pathway into legal education with a strong emphasis on advocacy, ethics and practical training. The programme, anchored by the slogan “Learn the Law. Master Advocacy. Lead with Integrity,” is designed to prepare students for diverse careers in law, including litigation, corporate practice, international organisations and non-governmental organisations. Speaking at the launch, the founding Dean of the Heritage School of Law, Prof. Kwadwo Appiagyei-Atua, said the programme would reflect HCU’s philosophy of combining conviction, creativity, community, compassion, ethics and entrepreneurship. He said the school sought to produce lawyers who combine strong academic training with an entrepreneurial mindset and a commitment to expanding access to justice. According to Prof. Appiagyei-Atua, the programme would adopt a student-centred approach , treating students as co-creators of knowledge while exposing them to practical legal work. The objective, he said, was to enable students to develop the skills and professional mindset required to begin thinking and working like lawyers even before completing their studies. Focus on practical legal education A major feature of the programme will be clinical legal education , through which students will gain practical experience while providing basic legal services to underserved communities. The university said the approach was intended to help address Ghana’s access-to-justice challenges, particularly among marginalised communities. The programme will also offer a broad range of elective courses, including sports law, entertainment law, tourism and hospitality law, maritime law, health law and education law. Prof. Appiagyei-Atua said the wide range of electives would allow students to align their legal education with their professional interests and existing areas of expertise. The school also plans to introduce French as a composite course to broaden students’ language skills and prepare them for opportunities in a wider international environment. Pathway for degree holders In addition to the undergraduate LLB programme for WASSCE/SSSCE holders, the university will offer a special programme for applicants who already hold first degrees in disciplines other than law. The initiative is intended to allow graduates from fields such as business, health, tourism, education and other professions to combine their existing expertise with legal training. Prof. Appiagyei-Atua said the school would also explore opportunities for students to combine law with other academic programmes, creating multidisciplinary qualifications that could expand their career options. He said the university was also working towards student mobility opportunities with institutions in the United States, allowing students to undertake semester- or year-long programmes abroad while earning credits towards their studies at HCU. Facilities and faculty The Heritage School of Law is situated on HCU’s campus at Amasaman in Accra, in a relatively quiet environment designed to support academic work. The university said the school has purpose-built facilities, including classrooms, moot court space, discussion areas and a dedicated law library in addition to access to the university’s main library. Prof. Appiagyei-Atua said the school was assembling an experienced faculty to provide students with quality legal education. He brings more than two decades of experience in legal education, having taught in institutions in Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Russia and South Africa. Admission The university said applicants could gain admission through several routes. WASSCE/SSSCE holders require at least six credits, including English Language, Core Mathematics and Integrated Science or Social Studies, together with three elective subjects. Applicants with a first degree from a GTEC-accredited university may be admitted to Level 200 , while holders of foreign or international qualifications must have their credentials evaluated by the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC). Mature applicants aged 25 or above at the beginning of the academic year, with relevant professional experience, will be required to pass an entrance examination in English Language and Core Mathematics, an aptitude test and an interview. Heritage Christian University said its law programme had also been structured with developments in Ghana’s legal education system in mind, with the aim of providing students with continuity from academic legal education into professional training. The university said graduates would have opportunities beyond traditional litigation and judicial careers, including work in the corporate sector, international organisations, non-governmental organisations and other specialised areas of legal practice. Heritage Christian University is a GTEC-accredited, faith-based chartered private university located at Amasaman, Accra. The Heritage School of Law is located on the university’s campus behind the Olympic Stadium, Amasaman. Prospective applicants can contact the university on +233 55 102 6164 or +233 20 229 8399 , or visit HCU’s website for further information.

items.title: Security, traffic plans for Eid Miladun Nabi processions
items.description: Elaborate security and road traffic arrangements were made by authorities across the country for rallies in connection with the 12th Rabiul Awwal on Wednesday. Karachi In Karachi, 4,208 policemen were deployed to secure religious rallies and gatherings in the metropolis, of whom 1,702 were stationed in South Zone and 765 in East Zone, according to an official statement by police. Police said 397 officers and personnel had been deployed for the security of the main 12th Rabiul Awwal procession at Nishtar Park, and 362 more had been stationed at the entry points of the park. Karachi Additional Inspector General Azad Khan, the metropolis’s police chief, had directed law enforcers to remain on high alert on routes of all processions, and traffic police had been instructed to ensure smooth flow of traffic, the statement said. He also issued directions for the effective monitoring of the security situation through CCTV cameras. Meanwhile, the city’s traffic police said three main processions were planned in the city. The first procession was scheduled to depart from Shaheed Masjid in Kharadar at 2:30pm, pass through Memon Masjid and conclude at Gulzar-i-Habib Mosque at the time of Asr prayers. The second was scheduled to depart from Memon Masjid at 2:30pm and conclude at Aram Bagh Masjid at the time of Asr prayers. The main procession was to depart from Memon Masjid after 3pm and conclude at Nishtar Park at around 6pm. Map of procession routes in Karachi — Traffic Police According to the traffic plan for the day, commuters travelling from Nazimabad were directed from Lasbela Chowk via Nishtar Road towards Garden. Those coming from Liaquatabad were advised to turn left at Teen Hatti and proceed towards Central Jail (Martin Road). Commuters travelling from Hassan Square towards PIB Colony used Kashmir Road to reach Society Light Signal (Shahrah-i-Quaideen). Those travelling from the Jail Flyover towards Teen Hatti took Nishtar Road via Lasbela Chowk. No traffic was allowed to travel from the Governor House towards Numaish. Commuters travelling from Sharea Faisal via Shahrah-i-Quaideen (Noorani Kabab) towards Numaish turned right at Society Light Signal onto Kashmir Road to reach their destinations. Those travelling from Central Jail Gate (Jamshed Road) via Gurumandir towards M.A. Jinnah Road used Gurumandir Bypass Road and Soldier Bazar. Commuters travelling from Garden Chowrangi towards M.A. Jinnah Road turned right at Anklesaria Hospital towards Gul Plaza, or turned left at Coast Guard/Holy Family Hospital to reach their destinations. Traffic coming from Lucky Star towards M.A. Jinnah Road and Empress Market was diverted from Saddar Dawakhana towards PP Chowrangi. Similarly, traffic heading towards Preedy Road was diverted from Abdullah Haroon Road towards M.A. Jinnah Chowk, from where it could proceed towards its destination. Traffic was not allowed to travel from M.A. Jinnah Chowk towards Court Road (Kabootar Chowk). All traffic was to be diverted via Strachan Road towards Pakistan Chowk. Traffic heading from Shahrah-i-Liaquat towards Preedy Road was diverted from Aram Bagh Light Signal towards Pakistan Chowk, from where it could proceed to its destination. Rawalpindi In Rawalpindi, more than 910 traffic police personnel were deployed to regulate traffic during the processions. A total of 120 processions were taken out across the city, including two categorised as A, 10 as B and 108 as C, according to the traffic police. Murree Road was closed in both directions during the processions. Traffic travelling from Rawalpindi to Islamabad were diverted via Tipu Road towards Liaquat Bagh Chowk while vehicles coming from Islamabad were diverted from the Rawal Road turn towards Rawal Road. Traffic travelling from Liaquat Bagh to Fawara Chowk were diverted from DAV College towards Gawalmandi. For the second procession, which started from Chungi No. 22, traffic coming from Kalma Chowk was diverted towards Harley Street. The procession passed through Tench Road, Dhoke Syedan Chowk, Kalma Chowk, No. 22 Chowk, Adiala Road, State Life Building turn, MH Chowk, Mahfuz Chowk, Mansehra Adda, Thana Cantt, Nishtar Street, Adamji Road, Mithu Khan Complex, Railway Road, Military Accounts and Kamran Market to conclude at GTS Chowk. Traffic heading towards Khattak Chowk, CMH and Tench was diverted towards Harley Street during the procession. When the procession reached Mall Road, traffic coming from Peshawar Road was diverted from Qasim Market towards Sher Khan Road, the traffic police said. Traffic travelling from Kutchery Chowk towards Peshawar Road was diverted from TM Chowk to Murree Road. Tractor trolleys, trailers and trucks were not allowed to enter the procession routes. No parking was allowed within 300 yards of the stage. A special traffic plan had also been prepared to facilitate ambulances, fire engines and other emergency vehicles. Traffic was diverted from highways where processions were held, while citizens had been advised to avoid unnecessary travel on procession routes, Chief Traffic Officer (CTO) Farhan Aslam said. Peshawar The main procession in Peshawar was held under the banner of Idara Tableeghul Islam. It started after Isha (night) prayers from Milad Chowk in the city and, after passing through its traditional routes, culminated at Qissa Khwani Bazaar where the main Mehfil-i-Milad was held. Several small processions were also taken out from Sikandar Pura, Qissa Khwani, Saddar, Kohati, Gulbahar and other areas. According to the plan prepared by the city’s traffic police, four superintendents of police, 12 deputy superintendents of police (DSP) and 600 personnel and wardens were deployed across the city. Citizens also got traffic updates via helpline 1915. Lahore According to Lahore traffic police, 16 DSPs, 45 sector in-charges and over 1,400 wardens and patrolling officers were deployed in the city, where two main processions were taken out. In addition, 172 rallies and 125 Milad gatherings were organised, the traffic police posted on X. Overall in Punjab, 8,000 traffic police officers and personnel were deployed across the province, according to a statement by the Punjab traffic police. It said 1,436 Miladun Nabi gatherings and 2,479 processions had been planned across the province, while 216 processions and 111 Milad gatherings would be held in Lahore. The Punjab Police deployed 55,000 personnel for about 4,500 gatherings and processions across the province for Eid Miladun Nabi. Punjab Inspector General of Police (IGP) Abdul Kareem said that the Counter-Terrorism Department would also monitor the main gatherings other than the field police officers, including regional and district police officers, across the province. He said that security would remain on high alert during the Eid Miladun Nabi programmes.

items.title: ASUU: State varsities in Plateau, Edo, Ondo, others begin strike
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Adesina Wahab, Ozioruva Aliu & Golok Nanmwa Academic activities have been disrupted in several state-owned universities across the country following the commencement of industrial action by members of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) over the non-implementation of provisions of the 2009 Re-negotiated Agreement. Checks by Vanguard on Wednesday showed that lecturers in several affected institutions complied with the directive of the union’s national leadership to withdraw their services. The affected universities include Nasarawa State University; Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida University, Lapai; Gombe State University; Plateau State University; Kaduna State University; Kano State University of Science and Technology; Northwest University; and Taraba State University. Others are the University of Medical Sciences, Ondo; Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko; Ambrose Alli University, Ekpoma; Olusegun Agagu University of Science and Technology; and Emmanuel Alayande University of Education. The list also includes Abia State University; University of Education and Entrepreneurship, Akamkpa; Enugu State University of Science and Technology; Imo State University; Niger Delta University; University of Africa, Toru-Orua; and Bayelsa Medical University. AAUA ASUU: No Going Back At Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko (AAUA), Ondo State, the branch of ASUU said it would not suspend the strike until the state government commenced implementation of the agreement and paid outstanding arrears dating back to January 2026. The branch chairman, Prof. Bolu Oshodi, said the union was demanding immediate implementation of the new salary structure, which took effect in January 2026. Oshodi said federal universities and some state-owned institutions, including Ekiti State University (EKSU), Benue State University (BSU), Osun State University (UNIOSUN), Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH) and Kwara State University (KWASU), had commenced implementation of the new package. The state government had subsequently indicated its willingness to implement the agreement, although the proposed payment would not cover all the outstanding arrears, according to the union. Oshodi said the branch would only suspend the strike after receiving payment of the implementation and arrears in its members’ bank accounts. “We will call off the strike when we receive alert in our bank accounts. Alert of the implementation and the arrears starting from January, that is when we will suspend the strike,” he said. He explained that the branch’s position was in line with the directive of the union’s national body, which directed that implementation of the agreement should commence immediately and that arrears owed to workers from January should also be paid. According to him, the union interprets “immediate” implementation to mean that outstanding obligations dating back to January should be settled. “The issue now is that the mandate from the national body is that the implementation should commence immediately and the arrears from January should be paid,” Oshodi said. PLASU ASUU Declares Indefinite Strike At Plateau State University, Bokkos (PLASU), ASUU members declared a total and indefinite strike over what they described as the failure of the university management to satisfactorily address their six-point charter of demands. In a statement signed by the branch chairperson, Vincent D. Choji, and Secretary, Lomka Iliya Kopdiya, and made available on Wednesday, the union said its demands remained unresolved despite the expiration of an ultimatum issued to the authorities. The demands include commencement of the Contributory Pension Scheme, full implementation of the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU agreement and payment of arrears from January 1, 2026. Others include the provision of safe and secure staff quarters, construction of trenches around the university’s perimeter fence and an end to what the union described as intimidation of its leaders. The union also demanded payment of 22 months’ arrears of the 25/35 per cent wage award. Academic Activities Grounded at AAU Academic activities were also disrupted at Ambrose Alli University (AAU), Ekpoma, Edo State, on Wednesday as ASUU members commenced an indefinite strike over the non-implementation of the agreement reached by the union’s national leadership. Students who spoke to Vanguard said only lecturers with administrative or other official engagements were seen on campus, while most lecturers’ offices remained closed. The university’s Public Relations Officer, Otunba Mike Aladenika, confirmed that the institution’s management was at the Edo State Government House for a meeting with Governor Monday Okpebholo. The university’s ASUU branch had, two days earlier, announced the commencement of the strike following a congress meeting. In a statement signed by the branch chairman and secretary, Dr Cyril Onogbosele and Dr William Odion, respectively, the union cited the non-implementation of the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU agreement and failure to pay accrued arrears of allowances under the agreement from January 2026. The union said the decision followed the expiration of a 14-day ultimatum issued to the university authorities and Edo State Government. “Having failed to implement the Agreement within the 14-day ultimatum in addition to unsuccessful efforts by the Branch to make the University authorities and Edo State Government to implement the Agreement, Congress resolved and directed members to embark on a total, comprehensive and indefinite strike with effect from Tuesday, 25th August, 2026 at 12.01am,” the statement said. The branch said the industrial action covered the withdrawal of statutory services by members, including teaching and lecturing, conduct and invigilation of examinations, statutory meetings, and supervision of students’ research projects, Industrial Training and Teaching Practice. The congress also mandated the branch executive to activate its strike monitoring team and directed members to comply with the resolutions. The post ASUU: State varsities in Plateau, Edo, Ondo, others begin strike appeared first on Vanguard News .
